title.zh: 卷九十三 志第六十九 刑法一
title.raw: 卷九十三 志第六十九 刑法一 Volume 93 Treatises 69: Punishment and Law 1

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，刑法沿革不一。

translations.literal: Since the Han, penal law has evolved without uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, criminal law underwent many changes and never settled into one consistent form.

sentences.zh: 隋更五刑之條，設三奏之令。

translations.literal: The Sui revised the provisions of the five punishments and established the ordinance of three presentations.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui revised the five punishments and required three separate memorials before execution could proceed.

sentences.zh: 唐撰律令，一準乎禮，以為出入。

translations.literal: The Tang compiled statutes and ordinances, taking ritual alone as the standard for deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang compiled its code and edicts, using ritual propriety alone as the measure for judgment and penalty.

sentences.zh: 宋採用之，而所重者敕。

translations.literal: The Song adopted them, yet what it valued was imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The Song adopted Tang law, but placed greater weight on imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 律所不載者，則聽之於敕。

translations.literal: What the code did not record was left to edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Matters not covered in the code were governed by edict instead.

sentences.zh: 故時輕時重，無一是之歸。

translations.literal: Thus punishments were sometimes light and sometimes heavy, with no single principle to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment therefore swung between leniency and severity, with no settled standard.

sentences.zh: 元制，取所行一時之例為條格而已。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan system, one took only the precedents in force at a given time as statutory rules.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan practice simply codified whatever precedents happened to be in use at the moment.

sentences.zh: 明初，丞相李善長等言：「歷代之律，皆以漢《九章》為宗，至唐始集其成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, Chancellor Li Shanchang and others said: "The codes of successive dynasties all took the Han Nine Chapters as their foundation, and only under the Tang did they take final form.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming, Chancellor Li Shanchang and others said, "Dynastic law codes have always looked back to the Han Nine Chapters; only under the Tang were they brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 今制宜遵唐舊。」

translations.literal: For present institutions, it is fitting to follow Tang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Our code should follow Tang precedent.

sentences.zh: 太祖從其言。

translations.literal: The Founder accepted their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 始，太祖懲元縱弛之後，刑用重典，然特取決一時，非以為則。

translations.literal: At first, the Founder, reacting to the Yuan's lax indulgence, used severe statutes in punishment, yet he took decisions only for the moment and did not treat them as fixed rules.
translations.idiomatic: At first, having seen how indulgent Yuan rule had become, the Founder imposed harsh penalties, but only as temporary measures, not as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 後屢詔釐正，至三十年，始申畫一之制，所以斟酌損益之者，至纖至悉，令子孫守之。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly ordered revisions, and by the thirtieth year he at last proclaimed a uniform system; what he weighed in adding or subtracting was minutely thorough, commanding his descendants to uphold it.
translations.idiomatic: He issued repeated orders to revise the law, and by the thirtieth year of his reign had established a single uniform code, refined in every detail, which he enjoined his descendants to uphold.

sentences.zh: 羣臣有稍議更改，即坐以變亂祖制之罪。

translations.literal: If ministers so much as discussed alteration, they were charged with the crime of disturbing the ancestral institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Any minister who so much as proposed a change was prosecuted for subverting the founder's institutions.

sentences.zh: 而後乃滋弊者，由於人不知律，妄意律舉大綱，不足以盡情偽之變，於是因律起例，因例生例，例愈紛而弊愈無窮。

translations.literal: The abuses that later proliferated arose because people did not understand the code and fancied that because it stated only broad principles it could not cover every turn of truth and fraud; thus from the code precedents arose, and from precedents more precedents, until precedents grew ever more confused and abuses ever without end.
translations.idiomatic: Later abuses stemmed from ignorance of the code: officials assumed its broad principles could not cover every variation in fact, so they built precedents upon the code and precedents upon precedents, until precedent piled upon precedent and abuse knew no end.

sentences.zh: 初詔內外風憲官，以講讀律令一條，考校有司。

translations.literal: At first an edict ordered censorial officials within and without to expound and study one provision of the statutes and ordinances and examine the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: An early edict required censorial officials inside and outside the capital each to study and explain one provision of the code, then to test officials under them.

sentences.zh: 其不能曉晰者，罰有差。

translations.literal: Those who could not understand clearly were penalized according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed were punished in proportion to their rank.

sentences.zh: 庶幾人知律意。

translations.literal: The hope was that people would know the intent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was that everyone would grasp the spirit of the law.

sentences.zh: 因循日久，視為具文。

translations.literal: As custom dragged on through the years, it was regarded as mere form.
translations.idiomatic: In time the edict became a dead letter.

sentences.zh: 由此奸吏骫法，任意輕重。

translations.literal: Hence corrupt clerks twisted the law and arbitrarily made punishments light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials could then bend the law and fix penalties as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 至如律有取自上裁、臨時處治者，因罪在八議不得擅自勾問、與一切疑獄罪名難定、及律無正文者設，非謂朝廷可任情生殺之也。

translations.literal: As for provisions in the code for taking decision from above or temporary disposition, these were established for cases within the eight deliberations that could not be questioned without authorization, for all doubtful cases where the charge was hard to fix, and where the code had no explicit text—not meaning that the court could arbitrarily give life or death.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions for imperial review or ad hoc disposition applied to cases within the eight deliberations that officials could not investigate on their own, to doubtful trials where the charge was unclear, and to matters the code did not expressly cover—they did not authorize the court to kill or spare at whim.

sentences.zh: 英、憲以後，欽恤之意微，偵伺之風熾。

translations.literal: After the Yingzong and Xianzong reigns, the spirit of merciful review waned and the wind of surveillance grew fierce.
translations.idiomatic: After the reigns of the Ying and Xian emperors, imperial clemency faded while informants and spies flourished.

sentences.zh: 巨惡大憝，案如山積，而旨從中下，從之不問。

translations.literal: Great evils and arch-criminals piled up in dossiers like mountains, yet edicts came from the center and were followed without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Monstrous crimes accumulated in vast dossiers, yet orders came down from above and were obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 或本無死理，而片紙付詔獄，為禍尤烈。

translations.literal: Some who by rights deserved no death, with a single slip of paper sent to the edict prison, suffered calamity still more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Men who deserved no death might be sent to the imperial prison on a single written order—a calamity worse still.

sentences.zh: 故綜明代刑法大略，而以廠衛終之。

translations.literal: Therefore this chapter summarizes the broad outline of Ming penal law, and ends with the palace prisons and guards.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is an overview of Ming criminal law, concluding with the palace prisons and guard establishments.

sentences.zh: 廠豎姓名，傳不備載，列之於此，使有所考焉。

translations.literal: The names of the eunuch agents of the prisons are not fully recorded in transmitted accounts; they are listed here so that there may be something to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch agents' names are incompletely preserved in older accounts; they are listed here for reference.

sentences.zh: 明太祖平武昌，即議律令。

translations.literal: When the Ming founder pacified Wuchang, he at once discussed statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he pacified Wuchang, the founding emperor began planning a legal code.

sentences.zh: 吳元年冬十月，命左丞相李善長為律令總裁官，參知政事楊憲、傅瓛，御史中丞劉基，翰林學士陶安等二十人為議律官，諭之曰：「法貴簡當，使人易曉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Wu, he appointed Left Chancellor Li Shanchang chief compiler of statutes and ordinances, with twenty others including Vice Grand Councillors Yang Xian and Fu Yong, Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji, and Hanlin Academician Tao An as drafters of the law, instructing them: "Law should be concise and plain, easy for people to understand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter of the Wu era's first year, he named Left Chancellor Li Shanchang to head the code commission, with twenty colleagues including Yang Xian, Fu Yong, Liu Ji, and Tao An as drafters, and told them: "Law ought to be plain and brief, so that anyone can understand it.

sentences.zh: 若條緒繁多，或一事兩端，可輕可重，吏得因緣為奸，非法意也。

translations.literal: If clauses are numerous, or one matter has two ends so that it may be treated lightly or heavily, clerks can seize the opportunity to commit fraud—this is not the intent of law.
translations.idiomatic: If the articles multiply, or one act can be read two ways and punished lightly or heavily, clerks will exploit the ambiguity—that is not what law is for.

sentences.zh: 夫網密則水無大魚，法密則國無全民。

translations.literal: When the net is dense, the water holds no large fish; when the law is dense, the state has no whole people.
translations.idiomatic: A net too fine leaves no large fish in the water; a code too dense leaves no innocent citizen in the realm.

sentences.zh: 卿等悉心參究，日具刑名條目以上，吾親酌議焉。」

translations.literal: You are to investigate with full care, daily submitting articles on criminal matters for my personal deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Study the matter carefully, submit criminal-law articles to me each day, and I will weigh them myself.

sentences.zh: 每禦西樓，召諸臣賜坐，從容講論律義。

translations.literal: Each time he went to the Western Tower, he summoned the ministers, granted them seats, and calmly discussed the meaning of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went to the Western Tower, he seated his ministers and discussed the meaning of the statutes at leisure.

sentences.zh: 十二月，書成，凡為令一百四十五條，律二百八十五條。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the work was completed, comprising in all 145 ordinances and 285 statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the code was finished: 145 ordinances and 285 statutes in all.

sentences.zh: 又恐小民不能周知，命大理卿周楨等取所定律令，自禮樂、制度、錢糧、選法之外，凡民間所行事宜，類聚成編，訓釋其義，頒之郡縣，名曰《律令直解》。

translations.literal: Fearing that common people could not know it fully, he ordered Chief Minister of Justice Zhou Zhen and others to take the statutes and ordinances enacted, and apart from rites and music, institutions, grain and tax, and selection law, to gather all matters practiced among the people into a compilation, explain their meaning, and distribute it to prefectures and counties under the title Direct Explanation of Statutes and Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ordinary people could not master the code, he had Chief Minister of Justice Zhou Zhen and others compile everything in daily civilian life—aside from ritual, institutions, revenue, and official selection—explain it plainly, and issue it to the counties as the Direct Explanation of Statutes and Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽其書而喜曰：「吾民可以寡過矣。」

translations.literal: The Founder read the book and said with pleasure: "My people can now commit few offenses."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor read it and said with delight, "My people will now seldom break the law."

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，又命儒臣四人，同刑官講《唐律》，日進二十條。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he again ordered four Confucian officials, together with penal officials, to lecture on the Tang Code, advancing twenty articles per day.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 he set four scholar-officials and penal officials to study the Tang Code together, covering twenty articles a day.

sentences.zh: 五年，定宦官禁令及親屬相容隱律，六年夏，刊《律令憲綱》，頒之諸司。

translations.literal: In year five he fixed prohibitions on eunuchs and the statute on mutual concealment among kin; in summer of year six he published the Constitutional Outline of Statutes and Ordinances and distributed it to all offices.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he enacted bans on eunuchs and rules on kin concealing one another's crimes; in the summer of year 6 he published the Constitutional Outline of Statutes and Ordinances and sent it to every agency.

sentences.zh: 其冬，詔刑部尚書劉惟謙詳定《大明律》。

translations.literal: That winter he ordered Minister of Justice Liu Weiqian to compile the Great Ming Code in detail.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he charged Minister of Justice Liu Weiqian with drafting the Great Ming Code.

sentences.zh: 每奏一篇，命揭兩廡，親加裁酌。

translations.literal: Whenever a section was submitted, he ordered it posted in both side halls and personally revised it.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a section arrived, he had it posted in the side halls and revised it himself.

sentences.zh: 及成，翰林學士宋濂為表以進，曰：「臣以洪武六年冬十一月受詔，明年二月書成。

translations.literal: When it was finished, Hanlin Academician Song Lian presented a memorial saying: "Your servant received the edict in the eleventh month of winter in the sixth year of Hongwu, and the book was completed in the second month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done, Hanlin Academician Song Lian submitted a memorial stating, "I received the order in the eleventh month of winter, Hongwu 6, and finished the code in the second month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 篇目一準於唐：曰衛禁，曰職制，曰戶婚，曰廄庫，曰擅興，曰賊盜，曰鬥訟，曰詐偽，曰雜律，曰捕亡，曰斷獄，曰名例。

translations.literal: The chapters followed the Tang exactly: Guard and Prohibition, Office Regulations, Household and Marriage, Stables and Storehouses, Unauthorized Enterprises, Banditry and Theft, Assault and Litigation, Fraud and Forgery, Miscellaneous Statutes, Apprehension of Fugitives, Trial and Punishment, and General Principles.
translations.idiomatic: Its chapters matched the Tang: Guard and Prohibition, Office Regulations, Household and Marriage, Stables and Storehouses, Unauthorized Enterprises, Banditry and Theft, Assault and Litigation, Fraud and Forgery, Miscellaneous Statutes, Apprehension of Fugitives, Trial and Punishment, and General Principles.

sentences.zh: 採用舊律二百八十八條，續律百二十八條，舊令改律三十六條，因事制律三十一條，掇《唐律》以補遺百二十三條，合六百有六條，分為三十卷。

translations.literal: It adopted 288 articles from the old code, added 128 new statutes, converted 36 old ordinances into statutes, made 31 statutes for particular matters, and drew 123 articles from the Tang Code to fill gaps, totaling 606 articles in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: It retained 288 old statutes, added 128 new ones, turned 36 ordinances into statutes, drafted 31 statutes for new matters, and borrowed 123 articles from the Tang Code to fill gaps—606 articles in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 或損或益，或仍其舊，務合輕重之宜。」

translations.literal: Some were reduced or increased, some kept as before, all striving to suit the balance of severity and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Some provisions were tightened, some relaxed, some left unchanged, all so that penalties would fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 九年，太祖覽律條猶有未當者，命丞相胡惟庸、御史大夫汪廣洋等詳議，釐正十有三條。

translations.literal: In year nine the Founder, finding some articles still unsuitable, ordered Chancellor Hu Weiyong, Censor-in-Chief Wang Guangyang, and others to deliberate and revise thirteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, finding some articles still unsatisfactory, the founding emperor had Chancellor Hu Weiyong, Censor-in-Chief Wang Guangyang, and others revise thirteen provisions.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命尚書開濟定詐偽律條。

translations.literal: In year sixteen he ordered Minister Kai Ji to fix the articles on fraud and forgery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he had Minister Kai Ji draft the fraud and forgery statutes.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，刑部言：「比年條例增損不一，以致斷獄失當。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two the Ministry of Justice said: "In recent years precedents have been added and cut inconsistently, causing improper judgments in trials.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 the Ministry of Justice reported, "Recent precedents have been revised inconsistently, leading to improper verdicts.

sentences.zh: 請編類頒行，俾中外知所遵守。」

translations.literal: We ask that they be compiled by category and promulgated, so that within and without all may know what to observe.
translations.idiomatic: Please compile and issue them by category so that everyone inside and outside the capital knows what to follow.

sentences.zh: 遂命翰林院同刑部官，取比年所增者，以類附入。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Hanlin Academy together with penal officials to take what had been added in recent years and attach it by category.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Hanlin Academy and penal officials to gather recent additions and insert them by category.

sentences.zh: 改《名例律》冠於篇首。

translations.literal: He changed the General Principles chapter to stand at the head of the work.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the General Principles chapter to the front of the code.

sentences.zh: 為卷凡三十，為條四百有六十。

translations.literal: There were thirty juan in all and 460 articles.
translations.idiomatic: The code comprised thirty volumes and 460 articles.

sentences.zh: 《名例》一卷，四十七條。

translations.literal: General Principles: one juan, forty-seven articles.
translations.idiomatic: General Principles: one volume, forty-seven articles.

sentences.zh: 《吏律》二卷，曰職制十五條，曰公式十八條。

translations.literal: Officials Code: two juan—Office Regulations fifteen articles, Administrative Formulas eighteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: Officials Code: two volumes—Office Regulations, fifteen articles; Administrative Formulas, eighteen articles.

sentences.zh: 《戶律》七卷，曰戶役十五條，曰田宅十一條，曰婚姻十八條，曰倉庫二十四條，曰課程十九條，曰錢債三條，曰市廛五條。

translations.literal: Household Code: seven juan—Household Service fifteen, Fields and Dwellings eleven, Marriage eighteen, Granaries and Storehouses twenty-four, Tax and Transit nineteen, Money and Debt three, Markets five.
translations.idiomatic: Household Code: seven volumes—Household Service (15), Fields and Dwellings (11), Marriage (18), Granaries and Storehouses (24), Tax and Transit (19), Money and Debt (3), Markets (5).

sentences.zh: 《禮律》二卷，曰祭祀六條，曰儀制二十條。

translations.literal: Rites Code: two juan—Sacrifices six articles, Ritual Institutions twenty articles.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Code: two volumes—Sacrifices, six articles; Ritual Institutions, twenty articles.

sentences.zh: 《兵律》五卷，曰宮衛十九條，曰軍政二十條，曰關津七條，曰廄牧十一條，曰郵驛十八條。

translations.literal: Military Code: five juan—Palace Guard nineteen, Military Administration twenty, Passes and Ferries seven, Stables and Herds eleven, Postal Stations eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Military Code: five volumes—Palace Guard (19), Military Administration (20), Passes and Ferries (7), Stables and Herds (11), Postal Stations (18).

sentences.zh: 《刑律》十一卷，曰盜賊二十八條，曰人命二十條，曰鬥毆二十二條，曰罵詈八條，曰訴訟十二條，曰受贓十一條，曰詐偽十二條，曰犯奸十條，曰雜犯十一條，曰捕亡八條，曰斷獄二十九條。

translations.literal: Penal Code: eleven juan—Banditry and Theft twenty-eight, Homicide twenty, Assault twenty-two, Abuse eight, Litigation twelve, Accepting Bribes eleven, Fraud and Forgery twelve, Adultery ten, Miscellaneous Offenses eleven, Apprehension of Fugitives eight, Trial and Punishment twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Penal Code: eleven volumes—Banditry and Theft (28), Homicide (20), Assault (22), Abuse (8), Litigation (12), Accepting Bribes (11), Fraud and Forgery (12), Adultery (10), Miscellaneous Offenses (11), Apprehension of Fugitives (8), Trial and Punishment (29).

sentences.zh: 《工律》二卷，曰營造九條，曰河防四條。

translations.literal: Works Code: two juan—Construction nine articles, River Control four articles.
translations.idiomatic: Works Code: two volumes—Construction, nine articles; River Control, four articles.

sentences.zh: 為五刑之圖凡二。

translations.literal: There were two diagrams of the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: There were two charts of the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 首圖五：曰笞，曰杖，曰徒，曰流，曰死。

translations.literal: The first chart had five: beating with the light stick, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, banishment, and death.
translations.idiomatic: The first chart listed five: beating with the light stick, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, banishment, and death.

sentences.zh: 笞刑五，自一十至五十，每十為一等加減。

translations.literal: Light-stick beating had five degrees, from ten to fifty blows, each ten constituting one grade of increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Light-stick beating had five grades, from ten to fifty strokes, increasing or decreasing by ten.

sentences.zh: 杖刑五，自六十至一百，每十為一等加減。

translations.literal: Heavy-stick beating had five degrees, from sixty to one hundred blows, each ten constituting one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy-stick beating had five grades, from sixty to one hundred strokes, in steps of ten.

sentences.zh: 徒刑五，徒一年杖六十，一年半杖七十，二年杖八十，二年半杖九十，三年杖一百，每杖十及徒半年為一等加減。

translations.literal: Penal servitude had five degrees: one year with sixty blows of the stick, one and a half years with seventy, two years with eighty, two and a half years with ninety, three years with one hundred; each ten blows of the stick and half year of servitude formed one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude had five grades: one year plus sixty strokes, one and a half years plus seventy, two years plus eighty, two and a half years plus ninety, three years plus one hundred—each extra ten strokes or half year marking one grade.

sentences.zh: 流刑三，二千里，二千五百里，三千里，皆杖一百，每五百里為一等加減。

translations.literal: Banishment had three degrees: two thousand li, two thousand five hundred li, and three thousand li, each with one hundred blows of the stick, each five hundred li forming one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment had three grades—2,000, 2,500, and 3,000 li—each with one hundred strokes; distance increased by five hundred li per grade.

sentences.zh: 死刑二，絞、斬。

translations.literal: Capital punishment had two forms: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment had two forms: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 五刑之外，徒有總徒四年，遇例減一年者，有準徒五年，斬、絞、雜犯減等者。

translations.literal: Beyond the five punishments, for servitude there was aggregate servitude of four years, and where precedent reduced one year; there was equivalent servitude of five years, and reduction of grade for decapitation, strangulation, and miscellaneous offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the five punishments, servitude could total four years, or five under equivalent sentencing; decapitation, strangulation, and miscellaneous offenses could be reduced by grade where precedent allowed.

sentences.zh: 流有安置，有遷徙，去鄉一千里，杖一百，準徒二年。

translations.literal: For banishment there was resettlement and relocation: one thousand li from one's native place, one hundred blows of the stick, equivalent to two years of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment included resettlement and relocation—one thousand li from home, one hundred strokes, equivalent to two years' servitude.

sentences.zh: 有口外為民，其重者曰充軍。

translations.literal: There was banishment beyond the passes to become a commoner; the heavier form was called military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Some offenders were sent beyond the frontier as commoners; the heavier penalty was military exile.

sentences.zh: 充軍者，明初唯邊方屯種。

translations.literal: Military exile at the beginning of Ming was only garrison farming on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming, military exile meant only frontier garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 後定制，分極邊、煙瘴、邊遠、邊衛、沿海、附近。

translations.literal: Later a fixed system divided destinations into the outermost frontier, miasma regions, remote borderlands, border garrisons, coastal areas, and nearby districts.
translations.idiomatic: Later regulations classified destinations as outer frontier, miasma belt, remote border, border garrison, coast, and nearby districts.

sentences.zh: 軍有終身，有永遠。

translations.literal: Exile could be for life or perpetual.
translations.idiomatic: Military exile could be for life or perpetual.

sentences.zh: 二死之外，有淩遲，以處大逆不道諸罪者。

translations.literal: Beyond the two forms of death there was slicing, used for crimes of great treason and impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Besides strangulation and decapitation there was death by slicing, reserved for treason and comparable crimes.

sentences.zh: 充軍、淩遲，非五刑之正，故圖不列。

translations.literal: Military exile and slicing were not among the orthodox five punishments, and so were not listed in the chart.
translations.idiomatic: Military exile and slicing were not part of the orthodox five punishments and therefore were omitted from the chart.

sentences.zh: 凡徒流再犯者，流者於原配處所，依工、樂戶留住法。

translations.literal: For all who reoffended after servitude or banishment, banished persons at their original assigned place followed the law on retaining artisan and musician households.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders in servitude or banishment were handled under the rules for retaining artisan and musician households at the original place of assignment.

sentences.zh: 三流並決杖一百，拘役三年。

translations.literal: All three degrees of banishment received one hundred blows of the stick and three years of close detention.
translations.idiomatic: All three banishment grades carried one hundred strokes and three years of close detention.

sentences.zh: 拘役者，流人初止安置，今加以居作，即唐、宋所謂加役流也。

translations.literal: Close detention meant that banished persons were at first only resettled, but now labor was added—what the Tang and Song called banishment with added labor.
translations.idiomatic: Close detention meant that exiles, once merely resettled, now also performed labor—the Tang and Song "banishment with added labor."

sentences.zh: 徒者於原役之所，依所犯杖數年限決訖，應役無得過四年。

translations.literal: Servitude offenders at the place of original labor, after the blows and term for the offense were decided, might serve no more than four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Servitude offenders served at the original place of assignment; once strokes and term were fixed, total labor could not exceed four years.

sentences.zh: 次圖七：曰笞，曰杖，曰訊杖，曰枷，曰杻，曰索，曰鐐。

translations.literal: The second chart had seven: light stick, heavy stick, interrogation stick, cangue, shackles, rope, and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: The second chart listed seven instruments: light stick, heavy stick, interrogation stick, cangue, shackles, rope, and fetters.

sentences.zh: 笞，大頭徑二分七釐，小頭減一分。

translations.literal: The light stick: the large end two fen seven li in diameter, the small end one fen less.
translations.idiomatic: The light stick's thick end measured two fen seven li in diameter; the thin end was one fen smaller.

sentences.zh: 杖，大頭徑三分二釐，小頭減如笞之數。

translations.literal: The heavy stick: the large end three fen two li in diameter, the small end reduced by the same amount as for the light stick.
translations.idiomatic: The heavy stick's thick end measured three fen two li; the thin end was reduced by the same proportion as the light stick.

sentences.zh: 笞、杖皆以荊條為之，皆臀受。

translations.literal: Light and heavy sticks were both made of thorn branches and both struck the buttocks.
translations.idiomatic: Both sticks were made of thorn branches and blows were applied to the buttocks.

sentences.zh: 訊杖，大頭徑四分五釐，小頭減如笞杖之數，以荊條為之，臀腿受。

translations.literal: The interrogation stick: large end four fen five li, small end reduced like the light and heavy sticks, made of thorn branches, striking buttocks and thighs.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogation stick's thick end measured four fen five li; the thin end followed the same reduction as the other sticks. It was made of thorn branches and struck buttocks and thighs.

sentences.zh: 笞、杖、訊，皆長三尺五寸，用官降式較勘，毋以筋膠諸物裝釘。

translations.literal: Light stick, heavy stick, and interrogation stick were all three chi five cun long, checked against the official model sent down, and not to be fitted with sinew, glue, or other materials.
translations.idiomatic: All three sticks were three chi five cun long, measured against the official pattern, and must not be reinforced with sinew, glue, or nails.

sentences.zh: 枷，自十五斤至二十五斤止，刻其上為長短輕重之數。

translations.literal: The cangue ranged from fifteen to twenty-five jin, with length and weight marked upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue weighed from fifteen to twenty-five jin, with length and weight marked on it.

sentences.zh: 長五尺五寸，頭廣尺五寸，杻長尺六寸，厚一寸，男子死罪者用之。

translations.literal: It was five chi five cun long, the head one chi five cun wide, the shackles one chi six cun long and one cun thick, used for men condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: It was five chi five cun long, with a head one chi five cun wide; shackles one chi six cun long and one cun thick were used for men sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 索，鐵為之，以系輕罪者，其長一丈。

translations.literal: The rope was of iron, used to bind those guilty of light offenses; it was one zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: The rope was iron, one zhang long, used to bind offenders guilty of minor crimes.

sentences.zh: 鐐，鐵連環之，以縶足，徒者帶以輸作，重三斤。

translations.literal: Fetters were iron links to bind the feet; servitude offenders wore them while performing labor; they weighed three jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fetters were iron rings for the feet; servitude offenders wore them during labor. They weighed three jin.

sentences.zh: 又為喪服之圖凡八：族親有犯，視服等差定刑之輕重。

translations.literal: There were also eight diagrams of mourning garments: when kinsmen offended, severity of punishment was fixed according to the gradations of mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: There were also eight mourning-garment charts: when relatives committed offenses, penalties were set according to mourning rank.

sentences.zh: 其因禮以起義者，養母、繼母、慈母皆服三年。

translations.literal: Where ritual gave rise to moral obligation, foster mother, stepmother, and loving mother all required three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Where ritual created moral obligation, foster mothers, stepmothers, and loving mothers all required three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 毆殺之，與毆殺嫡母同罪。

translations.literal: Beating or killing them was the same crime as beating or killing the principal mother.
translations.idiomatic: Assaulting or killing them carried the same penalty as assaulting or killing one's principal mother.

sentences.zh: 兄弟妻皆服小功，互為容隱者，罪得遞減。

translations.literal: Wives of brothers all wore five-month mourning; when they mutually concealed offenses for one another, punishment could be reduced step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Sisters-in-law wore five-month mourning; mutual concealment of offenses allowed stepwise reduction of punishment.

sentences.zh: 舅姑之服皆斬衰三年，毆殺罵詈之者，與夫毆殺罵詈之律同。

translations.literal: Parents-in-law all wore three-year unhemmed mourning; beating, killing, or reviling them followed the same statutes as for a husband beating, killing, or reviling.
translations.idiomatic: Parents-in-law required three-year unhemmed mourning; assaulting, killing, or abusing them was punished like assaulting, killing, or abusing one's husband.

sentences.zh: 姨之子、舅之子、姑之子皆緦麻，是曰表兄弟，不得相為婚姻。

translations.literal: Sons of the maternal aunt, sons of the maternal uncle, and sons of the paternal aunt all wore three-month mourning; these are called cousins on the mother's side and may not marry one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of one's maternal aunt, maternal uncle, and paternal aunt wore three-month mourning; as maternal cousins they could not intermarry.

sentences.zh: 大惡有十：曰謀反，曰謀大逆，曰謀叛，曰惡逆，曰不道，曰大不敬，曰不孝，曰不睦，曰不義，曰內亂。

translations.literal: There were ten great abominations: plotting rebellion, plotting great treason, plotting defection, wicked rebellion, impiety, great disrespect, unfilial conduct, discord within the clan, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ten great abominations were defined: plotting rebellion, plotting great treason, plotting defection, wicked rebellion, impiety, great disrespect, unfilial conduct, clan discord, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 雖常赦不原。

translations.literal: Even regular amnesties did not pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: Even ordinary amnesties did not cover them.

sentences.zh: 貪墨之贓有六：曰監守盜，曰常人盜，曰竊盜，曰枉法，曰不枉法，曰坐贓。

translations.literal: There were six kinds of corrupt gain: theft by supervisors and custodians, theft by ordinary persons, larceny, bending the law, not bending the law, and sitting on illicit goods.
translations.idiomatic: Six categories of corrupt gain were defined: theft by custodial officials, theft by ordinary persons, larceny, taking bribes by bending the law, taking bribes without bending the law, and passive receipt of illicit goods.

sentences.zh: 當議者有八：曰議親，曰議故，曰議功，曰議賢，曰議能，曰議勤，曰議貴，曰議賓。

translations.literal: Those subject to deliberation were eight: deliberation for kin, for old associates, for merit, for worth, for ability, for diligence, for rank, and for guests of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Eight categories required deliberation before punishment: imperial kin, old associates, merit, worth, ability, diligence, rank, and distinguished guests.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭太孫曰：「此書首列二刑圖，次列八禮圖者，重禮也。

translations.literal: The Founder instructed the heir apparent: "This book places the two penal charts first and the eight ritual charts next because ritual is valued.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor told the heir apparent, "This code opens with two penal charts and then eight ritual charts because ritual comes first.

sentences.zh: 顧愚民無知，若於本條下即注寬恤之令，必易而犯法，故以廣大好生之意，總列《名例律》中。

translations.literal: But ignorant common people, if lenient orders were annotated right under each article, would easily offend against the law; therefore the broad intent to cherish life was gathered altogether in the General Principles chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if leniency were noted under every article, ignorant people might take the law lightly and break it; so the emperor's mercy was gathered instead in the General Principles chapter.

sentences.zh: 善用法者，會其意可也。」

translations.literal: One skilled in using the law need only grasp its intent.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled judge need only grasp its intent.

sentences.zh: 太孫請更定五條以上，太祖覽而善之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent asked to revise more than five articles, and the Founder read them and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent proposed revising more than five articles, and the founding emperor approved them.

sentences.zh: 太孫又請曰：「明刑所以弼教，凡與五倫相涉者，宜皆屈法以伸情。」

translations.literal: The heir apparent again asked: "Clarifying punishment is how one assists instruction; wherever the five relationships are involved, the law should be bent to give scope to human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent added, "Clear penalties assist moral instruction; wherever the five relationships are involved, the law should yield to human feeling."

sentences.zh: 乃命改定七十三條，復諭之曰：「吾治亂世，刑不得不重。

translations.literal: ] Thereupon he ordered seventy-three articles revised, and again instructed him: "In my governance of a turbulent age, punishments could not but be severe.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered seventy-three articles revised and told him again, "When I ruled a turbulent age, punishments had to be severe.

sentences.zh: 汝治平世，刑自當輕，所謂刑罰世輕世重也。」

translations.literal: When you govern an age of peace, punishments should naturally be light—this is what is called punishments being light or heavy according to the age."
translations.idiomatic: When you govern an age of peace, punishments should naturally be lighter—that is what is meant by penalties varying in severity with the times.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，刑部言，律條與條例不同者宜更定。

translations.literal: ] In the twenty-fifth year, the Ministry of Justice reported that where statute articles and precedents differed, they ought to be revised.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the Ministry of Justice reported that statute articles and precedents that conflicted should be reconciled.

sentences.zh: 太祖以條例特一時權宜，定律不可改，不從。

translations.literal: The founding emperor held that precedents were merely temporary expedients of the moment, while the codified statutes could not be altered; he did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor held that precedents were only temporary measures, whereas the codified statutes could not be changed, and he refused.

sentences.zh: 三十年，作《大明律》誥成。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the proclamation completing the Great Ming Code was composed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, the proclamation completing the Great Ming Code was issued.

sentences.zh: 禦午門，諭羣臣曰：「朕仿古為治，明禮以導民，定律以繩頑，刊著為令。

translations.literal: He took the throne at the Meridian Gate and instructed the assembled officials: "I govern by imitating antiquity, clarifying ritual to guide the people, fixing laws to restrain the obstinate, and publishing them as ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: At the Meridian Gate he addressed the officials: "I govern by following antiquity—clarifying ritual to guide the people, fixing laws to restrain the stubborn, and publishing them as binding ordinances.

sentences.zh: 行之既久，犯者猶眾，故作《大誥》以示民，使知趨吉避兇之道。

translations.literal: After they had been in force for long, offenders were still numerous; therefore the Grand Pronouncements were composed to show the people, so they would know the way to seek fortune and avoid misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: After long enforcement offenders were still many, so he composed the Grand Pronouncements to show the people how to seek good fortune and avoid harm.

sentences.zh: 古人謂刑為祥刑，豈非欲民並生於天地間哉！

translations.literal: The ancients called punishment "auspicious punishment"—was it not that they wished the people all to live together between heaven and earth!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients called punishment the "auspicious penalty"—did they not mean for the people to live together under heaven and earth!

sentences.zh: 然法在有司，民不周知，故命刑官取《大誥》條目，撮其要略，附載於律。

translations.literal: Yet the law rested with the officials and the people did not fully know it; therefore he ordered the criminal officials to take the articles of the Grand Pronouncements, extract the essentials, and append them to the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the law lay with the magistrates and the people did not know it thoroughly, so he ordered the penal officials to take entries from the Grand Pronouncements, abridge the essentials, and append them to the Code.

sentences.zh: 凡榜文禁例悉除之，除謀逆及《律誥》該載外，其雜犯大小之罪，悉依贖罪例論斷，編次成書，刊佈中外，令天下知所遵守。」

translations.literal: All placard prohibitions and sundry rules were abolished; except for treason and what the Code and Proclamation covered, all miscellaneous offenses great and small were to be adjudicated according to the commutation precedents, arranged into a book, published at home and abroad, so all under heaven would know what to obey."
translations.idiomatic: All placard bans and ad hoc prohibitions were abolished; apart from treason and what the Code and Proclamation covered, every other offense great or small was to be judged under the commutation precedents, compiled into a book, and published throughout the realm so all would know what to follow."

sentences.zh: 《大誥》者，太祖患民狃元習，徇私滅公，戾日滋，十八年，採輯官民過犯，條為《大誥》。

translations.literal: As for the Grand Pronouncements: the founding emperor was distressed that the people clung to Yuan habits, favored private interest and harmed the public good, and offenses daily increased; in the eighteenth year he collected official and commoner transgressions and set them out as the Grand Pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Pronouncements arose because the founding emperor worried that the people clung to Yuan customs, put private gain above the public good, and offenses grew daily; in the eighteenth year he compiled official and popular misdeeds into the Grand Pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 其目十條：曰攬納戶，曰安保過付，曰詭寄田糧，曰民人經該不解物，曰灑派拋荒田土，曰倚法為奸，曰空引偷軍，曰黥刺在逃，曰官吏長解賣囚，曰寰中士夫不為君用。

translations.literal: Its categories were ten: tax-collection agents who intercept payments; security escorts who pass off responsibility; fraudulently registering land tax elsewhere; commoners who withhold what they ought to turn over; spreading assessments onto abandoned land; abusing the law to commit wrongdoing; falsely citing theft of soldiers; tattooing deserters who fled; officials and chief escorts who sell prisoners; and scholars throughout the realm who will not serve the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: It had ten headings: intercepting tax payments; security escorts who evade delivery; falsely registering land tax; withholding mandated goods; shifting levies onto abandoned fields; using the law to do evil; falsely reporting stolen soldiers; branding fugitives; officials and chief escorts who sell prisoners; and scholars empire-wide who refuse to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 其罪至抄劄。

translations.literal: Penalties for these went as far as confiscation of property and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties for these offenses could go as far as confiscation of property and execution.

sentences.zh: 次年復為《續編》、《三編》，皆頒學宮以課士，裏置塾師教之。

translations.literal: The next year he again produced the Supplementary Compilation and Third Compilation; all were distributed to state academies to examine scholars, and village tutors were appointed in hamlets to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he issued the Supplementary Compilation and Third Compilation; all were sent to state academies to test scholars, and village tutors were set up in communities to teach them.

sentences.zh: 囚有《大誥》者，罪減等。

translations.literal: Prisoners who possessed the Grand Pronouncements had their sentences reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners who owned a copy of the Grand Pronouncements had their sentences reduced by one degree.

sentences.zh: 於時，天下有講讀《大誥》師生來朝者十九萬餘人，並賜鈔遣還。

translations.literal: At the time, teachers and students throughout the realm who had lectured on the Grand Pronouncements and came to court numbered more than 190,000; all were given paper money and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than 190,000 teachers and students from across the empire who had lectured on the Grand Pronouncements came to court; all were given paper money and sent home.

sentences.zh: 自《律誥》出，而《大誥》所載諸峻令未嘗輕用。

translations.literal: Once the Code and Proclamation appeared, the severe ordinances recorded in the Grand Pronouncements were never lightly applied.
translations.idiomatic: After the Code and Proclamation were issued, the harsh commands recorded in the Grand Pronouncements were never applied lightly.

sentences.zh: 其後罪人率援《大誥》以減等，亦不復論其有無矣。

translations.literal: Afterwards offenders generally cited the Grand Pronouncements for commutation, without even discussing whether they possessed them.
translations.idiomatic: Later offenders routinely invoked the Grand Pronouncements to reduce their sentences, without anyone even asking whether they actually owned a copy.

sentences.zh: 大抵明律視唐簡核，而寬厚不如宋。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, Ming law was more concise and streamlined than Tang law, but not as lenient as Song law.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole Ming law was leaner and more streamlined than Tang law, but less generous than Song law.

sentences.zh: 至其惻隱之意，散見於各條，可舉一以推也。

translations.literal: As for its compassionate intent, scattered among the various articles, one example may be taken to infer the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Its compassionate intent appears scattered through the articles; one example is enough to infer the rest.

sentences.zh: 如罪應加者，必贓滿數乃坐。

translations.literal: For example, where punishment should be increased, one is not convicted until the illicit goods reach the full amount.
translations.idiomatic: For example, when a penalty should be increased, conviction requires that the stolen goods reach the full threshold.

sentences.zh: 如監守自盜，贓至四十貫絞。

translations.literal: For example, supervising guards who steal what they guard—when stolen goods reach forty strings, strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: For example, a supervising guard who steals what he guards faces strangulation when the stolen goods reach forty strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 若止三十九貫九十九文，欠一文不坐也。

translations.literal: If only thirty-nine strings ninety-nine wen, one wen short—no conviction.
translations.idiomatic: If the amount is only thirty-nine strings and ninety-nine wen, one wen short of the limit—no conviction.

sentences.zh: 加極於流三千里，以次增重，終不得至死。

translations.literal: Increase stops at exile three thousand li; each step adds severity, but never reaches death.
translations.idiomatic: Aggravation stops at exile three thousand li; each step adds severity but never reaches the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 而減至流者，自死而之生，無絞斬之別。

translations.literal: When reduced to exile, one goes from death to life, without distinction between strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: When a sentence is reduced to exile, the offender moves from death to life, with no distinction between strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 即唐律稱加就重條。

translations.literal: This is Tang law's article on increasing punishment by applying the heavier statute.
translations.idiomatic: This corresponds to the Tang Code article on applying the heavier statute when increasing punishment.

sentences.zh: 稱日者以百刻，稱年者以三百六十日。

translations.literal: A "day" is reckoned as one hundred ke; a "year" as three hundred sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: A "day" is counted as one hundred quarter-hours; a "year" as three hundred sixty days.

sentences.zh: 如人命辜限及各文書違限，雖稍不及一時刻，仍不得以所限之年月科罪，即唐例稱日以百刻條。

translations.literal: For homicide limitation periods and various document deadline violations, even if slightly short of one quarter-hour, one still may not punish by the full limit of years or months—this is Tang precedent's article on reckoning days by one hundred ke.
translations.idiomatic: For homicide limitation periods and various document deadlines, even if the delay falls slightly short of one quarter-hour, one still may not punish by the full limit in years or months—this follows the Tang precedent on counting days by one hundred quarter-hours.

sentences.zh: 未老疾犯罪，而事發於老疾，以老疾論；

translations.literal: If one committed a crime before old age or infirmity but the matter came to light during old age or infirmity, he is judged as old or infirm;
translations.idiomatic: If someone committed a crime before old age or infirmity but the matter came to light when he was old or infirm, he is judged as old or infirm;

sentences.zh: 幼小犯罪，而事發於長大，以幼小論。

translations.literal: if one committed a crime while young and small but the matter came to light after reaching maturity, he is judged as young and small.
translations.idiomatic: if someone committed a crime as a child but the matter came to light after he had grown up, he is judged as a child.

sentences.zh: 即唐律老小廢疾條。

translations.literal: This is Tang law's article on the young, the old, and the disabled.
translations.idiomatic: This corresponds to the Tang Code article on the young, the old, and the disabled.

sentences.zh: 犯死罪，非常赦所不原，而祖父母、父母老無養者，得奏聞取上裁。

translations.literal: For capital crimes not excluded from ordinary amnesties, if grandparents or parents are old and without support, one may memorialize for the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: For capital crimes not excluded from ordinary amnesties, if grandparents or parents are elderly and without support, the offender may petition for the emperor's ruling.

sentences.zh: 犯徒流者，餘罪得收贖，存留養親。

translations.literal: For penal servitude or exile, remaining offenses may be redeemed and the offender retained to support parents.
translations.idiomatic: For penal servitude or exile, remaining offenses may be commuted by ransom so the offender may stay home to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 即唐律罪非十惡條。

translations.literal: This is Tang law's article on crimes not among the Ten Abominations.
translations.idiomatic: This corresponds to the Tang Code article on crimes not among the Ten Abominations.

sentences.zh: 功臣及五品以上官禁獄者，許令親人入侍，徒流者並聽隨行，違者罪杖。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials and officials of fifth rank and above held in prison were permitted to have kin attend them; those sentenced to penal servitude or exile were also allowed attendants; violators were punished with beating.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials and officials of fifth rank and above in custody were allowed relatives to attend them; those sentenced to penal servitude or exile could also have attendants; violators were beaten.

sentences.zh: 同居親屬有罪，得互相容隱。

translations.literal: Cohabiting kin who committed crimes might conceal one another.
translations.idiomatic: Cohabiting relatives who committed crimes were permitted to conceal one another.

sentences.zh: 即唐律同居相容隱條。

translations.literal: This is Tang law's article on mutual concealment among cohabiting kin.
translations.idiomatic: This corresponds to the Tang Code article on mutual concealment among cohabiting kin.

sentences.zh: 奴婢不得首主。

translations.literal: Bondservants and maidservants might not accuse their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Bondservants and maidservants were forbidden to accuse their masters.

sentences.zh: 凡告人者，告人祖父不得指其子孫為證，弟不證兄，妻不證夫，奴婢不證主。

translations.literal: In all accusations, the accuser's grandfather might not name his grandchildren as witnesses; younger brothers might not testify against elder brothers, wives against husbands, or bondservants against masters.
translations.idiomatic: In all accusations, a plaintiff's grandfather could not name his grandchildren as witnesses; younger brothers could not testify against elder brothers, wives against husbands, or bondservants against masters.

sentences.zh: 文職責在奉法，犯杖則不敘。

translations.literal: Civil officials were charged with upholding the law; if punished by beating they were not ranked for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials were duty-bound to uphold the law; if sentenced to beating they were not considered for promotion.

sentences.zh: 軍官至徒流，以世功猶得擢用。

translations.literal: Military officials, even to penal servitude or exile, might still be promoted on hereditary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials, even when sentenced to penal servitude or exile, could still be promoted on hereditary merit.

sentences.zh: 凡若此類，或間採唐律，或更立新制，所謂原父子之親，立君臣之義以權之者也。

translations.literal: In all such cases, some occasionally drew on Tang law, others newly established regulations—what is called weighing by the principle of honoring the bond between father and son and establishing the bond between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: In all such cases the code sometimes borrowed from Tang law and sometimes created new rules—what is meant by weighing cases through the bonds of father and son and the obligations of ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 建文帝即位，諭刑官曰：「《大明律》，皇祖所親定，命朕細閱，較前代往往加重。

translations.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor took the throne, he instructed the criminal officials: "The Great Ming Code was personally fixed by the imperial founder; he ordered me to review it in detail. Compared with earlier dynasties, it is often heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen Emperor acceded, he told the penal officials: "The Great Ming Code was personally set by our founding emperor, who ordered me to review it closely. Compared with earlier dynasties it is often harsher.

sentences.zh: 蓋刑亂國之典，非百世通行之道也。

translations.literal: For punishment is the classic of a chaotic state, not a Way that passes through all generations.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is the law of a troubled age, not a code meant to endure for all generations.

sentences.zh: 朕前所改定，皇祖已命施行。

translations.literal: The revisions I made earlier the founding emperor has already ordered put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The revisions I proposed earlier the founding emperor has already ordered into effect.

sentences.zh: 然罪可矜疑者，尚不止此。

translations.literal: Yet cases where guilt is doubtful and deserving of compassion extend beyond these.
translations.idiomatic: Yet cases where guilt is doubtful and deserving of compassion go beyond even these.

sentences.zh: 夫律設大法，禮順人情，齊民以刑，不若以禮。

translations.literal: Law sets forth great principles; ritual accords with human feeling. To harmonize the people by punishment is inferior to doing so by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Law sets great principles; ritual accords with human feeling. Harmonizing the people through ritual is better than doing so through punishment.

sentences.zh: 其諭天下有司，務崇禮教，赦疑獄，稱朕嘉與萬方之意。」

translations.literal: Instruct all officials under heaven to honor ritual teaching, pardon doubtful cases, and express my wish to rejoice with the myriad regions."
translations.idiomatic: Instruct all officials throughout the realm to honor ritual teaching, pardon doubtful cases, and express my wish to share joy with all the world.

sentences.zh: 成祖詔法司問囚，一依《大明律》擬議，毋妄引榜文條例為深文。

translations.literal: ] The Chengzu Emperor decreed that when the judicial offices interrogated prisoners, they should deliberate wholly according to the Great Ming Code and not recklessly cite placard texts and precedents as harsh constructions.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu Emperor decreed that when judicial offices tried prisoners they must deliberate solely under the Great Ming Code and not recklessly cite placard texts and precedents to construct harsh charges.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，定誣告法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the law on false accusation was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle, the law on false accusation was established.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，又令讞囚者一依正律，盡革所有條例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, it was again ordered that those reviewing prisoners should follow the orthodox statutes alone and abolish all precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua, it was again ordered that those reviewing prisoners must follow the orthodox statutes alone and abolish all precedents entirely.

sentences.zh: 十五年，南直隸巡撫王恕言：「《大明律》後，有《會定見行律》百有八條，不知所起。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Wang Su, grand coordinator of South Zhili, said: "After the Great Ming Code there is the Consolidated Code in Current Use with 108 articles, of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Wang Su, grand coordinator of South Zhili, reported: "After the Great Ming Code there circulated a Consolidated Code in Current Use of 108 articles, of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 如《兵律》多支廩給，《刑律》罵制使及罵本管長官條，皆輕重失倫。

translations.literal: For example, the Military Code section on excessive disbursement of rations, and the Criminal Code sections on reviling imperial commissioners and reviling one's immediate superior—all have penalties disproportionate in severity.
translations.idiomatic: For example, the Military Code section on excessive ration payments and the Criminal Code sections on reviling imperial commissioners and one's immediate superior all assign penalties out of proportion to the offense.

sentences.zh: 流傳四方，有誤官守。

translations.literal: Circulated in all directions, they mislead officials in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Circulated everywhere, they mislead officials in the performance of their duties.

sentences.zh: 乞追板焚毀。」

translations.literal: I beg that the printing blocks be recalled and burned."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the printing blocks be recalled and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 命即焚之，有依此律出入人罪者，以故論。

translations.literal: ] He was ordered to burn them at once; anyone who, relying on this code, wrongly convicted or acquitted was to be judged for intentional offense.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered them burned immediately; anyone who relied on this code to wrongfully convict or acquit would be punished for intentional misconduct.

sentences.zh: 十八年，定挾詐得財罪例。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the precedent on obtaining property by coercion and fraud was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the precedent on obtaining property through coercion and fraud was established.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，去定律時已百年，用法者日弛。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, a century had passed since the statutes were fixed, and those who applied the law grew daily lax.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, a century had passed since the statutes were codified, and enforcement grew laxer by the day.

sentences.zh: 五年，刑部尚書彭韶等以鴻臚少卿李鐩請，刪定《問刑條例》。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Minister of Justice Peng Shao and others, at the request of Vice Minister of Ceremonial Li Zan, revised and fixed the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Minister of Justice Peng Shao and others, at the request of Vice Minister of Ceremonial Li Zan, revised the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents.

sentences.zh: 至十三年，刑官復上言：「洪武末，定《大明律》，後又申明《大誥》，有罪減等，累朝遵用。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year, the criminal officials again memorialized: "At the end of Hongwu the Great Ming Code was fixed; afterwards the Grand Pronouncements were clarified, and guilt could be reduced one grade—successive reigns have followed this.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirteenth year the penal officials memorialized again: "At the end of Hongwu the Great Ming Code was fixed; later the Grand Pronouncements were clarified so sentences could be reduced one degree, and successive reigns have followed this practice.

sentences.zh: 其法外遺奸，列聖因時推廣之而有例，例以輔律，非以破律也。

translations.literal: Where the law left gaps for lingering wrongdoing, successive sage emperors expanded it according to the times and there were precedents; precedents were to assist the statutes, not to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Where the law left gaps for lingering wrongdoing, successive emperors expanded it as times required, producing precedents meant to support the statutes, not override them.

sentences.zh: 乃中外巧法吏或借便己私，律浸格不用。」

translations.literal: Yet crafty legal officials at court and in the provinces sometimes exploited them for private advantage, and the statutes were gradually set aside and unused."
translations.idiomatic: Yet crafty legal officials at court and in the provinces sometimes exploited them for private gain, and the statutes were gradually set aside.

sentences.zh: 於是下尚書白昂等會九卿議，增歷年問刑條例經久可行者二百九十七條。

translations.literal: ] Thereupon Minister Bai Ang and others were ordered to confer with the Nine Ministers; they added 297 Interrogation of Criminals precedents from over the years that had long proved workable.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Minister Bai Ang and others to confer with the Nine Ministers; they added 297 Interrogation of Criminals precedents from over the years that had proved durable in practice.

sentences.zh: 帝摘其中六事，令再議以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor picked out six matters among them and ordered further deliberation before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor singled out six items and ordered further deliberation before reporting back.

sentences.zh: 九卿執奏，乃不果改。

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers held firmly to their memorial; in the end no changes were made.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers held to their memorial, and in the end no changes were made.

sentences.zh: 然自是以後，律例並行而網亦少密。

translations.literal: Yet from this time forward statutes and precedents operated in parallel, and the net grew somewhat tighter.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward statutes and precedents operated in parallel, and the legal net grew somewhat tighter.

sentences.zh: 王府禁例六條，諸王無故出城有罰，其法尤嚴。

translations.literal: Six forbidden rules for princely establishments: princes who left the city without cause were punished—the law was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: Six forbidden rules for princely establishments penalized princes who left their cities without cause; that law was especially strict.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，保定巡撫王應鵬言：「正德間，新增問刑條例四十四款，深中情法，皆宜編入。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Wang Yingpeng, grand coordinator of Baoding, said: "During Zhengde, forty-four new Interrogation of Criminals precedents were added; they fit human feeling and law deeply and should all be compiled in."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Wang Yingpeng, grand coordinator of Baoding, reported: "During the Zhengde reign forty-four new Interrogation of Criminals precedents were added; they strike the right balance of justice and feeling and should all be incorporated.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: ] The court did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not assent.

sentences.zh: 惟詔偽造印信及竊盜三犯者不得用可矜例。

translations.literal: Only for forging imperial seals by edict and for thieves who stole three times might the commutation for deserving compassion not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Only forgery of imperial seals by edict and theft committed three times were excluded from commutation on grounds of deserving compassion.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書胡世甯又請編斷獄新例，亦命止依律文及弘治十三年所欽定者。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Hu Shining again requested compilation of new precedents for adjudicating cases; he was also ordered to rely only on the statutory text and what had been imperially approved in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Hu Shining also asked to compile new case precedents; he was likewise ordered to rely only on the statutory text and what had been imperially approved in Hongzhi 13.

sentences.zh: 至二十八年，刑部尚書喻茂堅言：「自弘治間定例，垂五十年。

translations.literal: By the twenty-eighth year, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian said: "Since the precedents were fixed in Hongzhi, nearly fifty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-eighth year, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian reported: "Since the precedents were fixed in the Hongzhi reign, nearly fifty years have passed.

sentences.zh: 乞敕臣等會同三法司，申明《問刑條例》及嘉靖元年後欽定事例，永為遵守。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty command us to confer with the Three Judicial Offices, clarify the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents and the imperially approved cases after the first year of Jiajing, and make them permanently binding.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order us to confer with the Three Judicial Offices, clarify the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents and the imperially approved cases after Jiajing 1, and make them permanently binding.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年以後、嘉靖元年以前事例，雖奉詔革除，顧有因事條陳，擬議精當可採者，亦宜詳檢。

translations.literal: Cases from after the thirteenth year of Hongzhi to before the first year of Jiajing, though abolished by imperial edict, yet among those submitted on particular matters with deliberations finely judged and worth adopting—these too should be carefully examined.
translations.idiomatic: Cases from after Hongzhi 13 to before Jiajing 1, though abolished by edict, may include memorials on particular matters whose deliberations were sound and worth adopting; these too should be carefully reviewed.

sentences.zh: 若官司妄引條例，故入人罪者，當議黜罰。」

translations.literal: If officials recklessly cited precedents and intentionally wrongfully convicted, dismissal and punishment should be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: If officials recklessly cited precedents to wrongfully convict someone, dismissal and punishment should be considered.

sentences.zh: 會茂堅去官，詔尚書顧應祥等定議，增至二百四十九條。

translations.literal: ] When Maojian left office, Minister Gu Yingxiang and others were ordered to fix the deliberation; the total was increased to 249 articles.
translations.idiomatic: When Maojian left office, Minister Gu Yingxiang and others were ordered to finalize the code; the total was raised to 249 articles.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，又因尚書何ＢＩ言，增入九事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, because Minister He Bin spoke, nine further matters were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, at Minister He Bin's recommendation, nine further items were added.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，給事中烏昇請續增條例。

translations.literal: During Wanli, Supervising Secretary Wu Sheng requested continued additions to the precedents.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Supervising Secretary Wu Sheng asked to continue adding precedents.

sentences.zh: 至十三年，刑部尚書舒化等乃輯嘉靖三十四年以後詔令及宗籓軍政條例、捕盜條格、漕運議單與刑名相關者，律為正文，例為附註，共三百八十二條，刪世宗時苛令特多。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year, Minister of Justice Shu Hua and others compiled edicts after the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing and regulations on imperial clans, military administration, bandit capture, grain transport memorials, and all matters related to criminal law—statutes as main text, precedents as appended notes—382 articles in all, deleting many harsh commands from the Shizong reign in particular.
translations.idiomatic: By the thirteenth year, Minister of Justice Shu Hua and others compiled edicts after Jiajing 34 together with regulations on imperial clans, military administration, bandit capture, grain transport, and all matters touching criminal law—statutes as main text, precedents as marginal notes—382 articles in all, cutting many of the especially harsh commands from the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年，刑部尚書劉澤深復請議定《問刑條例》。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, Minister of Justice Liu Zeshen again requested deliberation to fix the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, Minister of Justice Liu Zeshen again asked for deliberation to fix the Interrogation of Criminals Precedents.

sentences.zh: 帝以律應恪遵，例有上下，事同而二三其例者，刪定畫一為是。

translations.literal: The emperor held that statutes should be strictly observed, but precedents had higher and lower authority; where the same matter had two or three precedents, revision to a single standard was right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that statutes must be strictly observed, but precedents had varying authority; where the same matter had two or three conflicting precedents, revision to a single standard was right.

sentences.zh: 然時方急法，百司救過不暇，議未及行。

translations.literal: Yet at the time harsh law was urgent; the hundred offices had no leisure to remedy faults, and the deliberation was not carried out in time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet harsh law enforcement was urgent at the time; the hundred offices were too busy covering their mistakes for the deliberation to be carried out.

sentences.zh: 太祖之定律文也，歷代相承，無敢輕改。

translations.literal: As for the founding emperor's fixing of the statutory text, successive generations inherited it and none dared lightly alter it.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's statutory text was handed down through successive reigns, and none dared alter it lightly.

sentences.zh: 其一時變通，或由詔令，或發於廷臣奏議，有關治體，言獲施行者，不可以無詳也。

translations.literal: Its temporary adaptations, whether by imperial edict or arising from court ministers' memorials, bearing on the foundations of governance and put into effect—these cannot go without full account.
translations.idiomatic: Its temporary adaptations, whether by edict or by memorials from court ministers, that bore on the foundations of governance and were put into effect cannot go unrecorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，諭省臣：「鞫獄當平恕，古者非大逆不道，罪止及身。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, he instructed the provincial officials: "In trying cases one should be even-handed and lenient. In antiquity, except for great treason and impiety, guilt stopped at the person.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu he instructed the provincial officials: "Trials should be even-handed and lenient. In antiquity, except for great treason, guilt stopped at the offender himself.

sentences.zh: 民有犯者，毋得連坐。」

translations.literal: When the people commit offenses, collective punishment must not be applied."
translations.idiomatic: When the people commit offenses, collective punishment is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏恕嘗引漢法，請著律，反者夷三族。

translations.literal: ] Minister Xia Shu once cited Han law and requested it be written into the Code: rebels were to have three clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xia Shu once cited Han law and asked that it be written into the Code: rebels were to have three clans exterminated.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「古者父子兄弟罪不相及，漢仍秦舊，法太重。」

translations.literal: The founding emperor said: "In antiquity fathers and sons, brothers, did not implicate one another in guilt. Han followed Qin custom—the law was too heavy."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said: "In antiquity fathers and sons and brothers did not implicate one another in guilt. Han followed Qin custom—the law was too harsh.

sentences.zh: 卻其奏不行。

translations.literal: ] He rejected the memorial and did not implement it.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected the memorial and did not implement it.

sentences.zh: 民父以誣逮，其子訴於刑部，法司坐以越訴。

translations.literal: A commoner's father was seized on a false charge; his son appealed to the Ministry of Justice, and the judicial office convicted him of improper appeal.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner's father was arrested on a false charge; his son appealed to the Ministry of Justice, and the judicial office convicted him of improper appeal.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「子訴父枉，出於至情，不可罪。」

translations.literal: The founding emperor said: "A son appealing his father's wrong arises from utmost feeling—it cannot be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said: "A son who appeals his father's injustice acts from deepest feeling—he cannot be punished.

sentences.zh: 有子犯法，父賄求免者，御史欲並論父。

translations.literal: ] When a son violated the law and his father bribed officials to seek exemption, the censor wanted to punish the father as well.
translations.idiomatic: When a son broke the law and his father bribed officials to secure his release, the censor wanted to punish the father as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「子論死，父救之，情也，但論其子，赦其父。」

translations.literal: The founding emperor said: "The son is sentenced to death and the father saves him—this is feeling. Judge only the son and pardon the father."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said: "The son faces death and the father tries to save him—that is human feeling. Judge only the son and pardon the father.

sentences.zh: 十七年，左都御史詹徽奏民毆孕婦至死者，律當絞，其子乞代。

translations.literal: ] In the seventeenth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui memorialized that a commoner who beat a pregnant woman to death should be strangled by law, and his son begged to die in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui reported that a commoner who beat a pregnant woman to death deserved strangulation by law, and the man's son begged to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 大理卿鄒俊議曰：「子代父死，情可矜。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zou Jun deliberated: "A son dying in his father's place—his feeling is deserving of compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zou Jun argued: "A son who dies in his father's place acts from feeling that deserves compassion.

sentences.zh: 然死婦系二人之命，犯人當二死之條，與其存犯法之人，孰若全無辜之子。」

translations.literal: Yet the dead woman involved two lives; the offender falls under the article for two deaths. Rather than spare the law-breaking man, is it not better to preserve the innocent son?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dead woman carried two lives; the offender falls under the statute for two deaths. Rather than spare the guilty man, is it not better to preserve the innocent son?

sentences.zh: 詔從後議。

translations.literal: ] An edict followed the latter deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the latter argument.

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Zhan Hui said: "A soldier who should be beaten for an offense had twice been guilty and pardoned; his prior crimes should be judged together and he should be executed."
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Zhan Hui said: "A soldier due for beating had twice been guilty and pardoned; his prior crimes should be judged together and he should be executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「前罪既宥，復論之則不信矣。」

translations.literal: ] The founding emperor said: "The prior crimes were already pardoned; to judge them again would be faithless."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said: "His prior crimes were already pardoned; to judge them again would break faith.

sentences.zh: 杖而遣之。

translations.literal: ] He was beaten and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten and sent away.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，嘉興通判龐安獲鬻私鹽者送京師，而以鹽賞獲者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Assistant Magistrate Pang An of Jiaxing apprehended sellers of illicit salt and sent them to the capital, using the salt as reward for the captor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Pang An, assistant magistrate of Jiaxing, arrested illicit salt dealers and sent them to the capital, rewarding the captor with the seized salt.

sentences.zh: 戶部以其違例，罰償鹽入官，且責取罪狀。

translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue ruled that he had broken regulations, fined him to repay the salt to the state, and demanded a written confession of guilt.

translations.idiomatic: Pang An argued: "The Code is eternal law; precedents are the policy of the moment.

translations.literal: If one now wishes to act by precedent, then as to the Code's words that reward is not given to those who ought not to be seized, one would contradict oneself and lose faith with all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If we now follow precedent instead, we contradict the Code's rule that rewards are not paid for seizing the wrong persons—and we would break faith with the realm.

sentences.zh: 太祖然其言，詔如律。

translations.literal: ] The founding emperor approved his words and ordered that the matter follow the Code.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor agreed and decreed that the case be decided according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，刑部言河間民訟其母，有司反擬母罪。

translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign, the Ministry of Punishments reported that a man in Hejian had sued his mother, yet local officials instead drafted charges against her.

sentences.zh: 詔執其子及有司罪之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the son and the officials be arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the son and the officials arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 三年，定文職官及中外旗校軍民人等，凡犯重條，依律科斷，輕者免決，記罪。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was fixed that civil officials and military and civilian personnel inside and outside the realm who committed grave articles should be sentenced according to the Code; minor offenders were exempted from beating and had their crime recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, a rule was set: civil officials and all military and civilian personnel at home and abroad who committed serious offenses were to be sentenced under the Code; minor cases were exempted from corporal punishment and only recorded.

sentences.zh: 其有不應侵損於人等項及情犯重者，臨時奏請。

translations.literal: Where there were items such as improper harm to persons or circumstances of grave offense, they were to memorialize for imperial decision at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving improper injury to others or grave circumstances were to be memorialized for the throne's decision.

sentences.zh: 十六年，嚴犯贓官吏之禁。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, prohibitions against corrupt officials were strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the ban on corrupt officials was strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖重懲貪吏，詔犯贓者無貸。

translations.literal: Initially, the founding emperor heavily punished greedy officials and decreed that those guilty of bribery would receive no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: At first the founding emperor punished greedy officials severely and decreed that bribe-takers would receive no mercy.

sentences.zh: 復敕刑部：「官吏受贓者，並罪通賄之人，徙其家於邊。

translations.literal: He again commanded the Ministry of Punishments: "Officials who accept bribes shall together be punished with those who bribed them, and their families shall be moved to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered the Ministry of Punishments: "Officials who take bribes shall be punished together with those who bribed them, and their families shall be relocated to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 著為令。」

translations.literal: Establish this as a statute."
translations.idiomatic: Make this a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 日久法弛，故復申飭之。

translations.literal: ] As time passed the law grew lax, so it was again vigorously enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the law had slackened, so it was enforced again.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，大理卿虞謙言：「誑騙之律，當杖而流，今梟首，非詔書意。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yu Qian said: "The statute on swindling should bring beating and exile; now decapitation is imposed, which is not the intent of the edict."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Chief Minister Yu Qian of the Court of Judicial Review said: "Swindling should be punished with beating and exile, yet now offenders are decapitated—this is not what the edict intended.

sentences.zh: 命如律擬斷。

translations.literal: ] He was ordered to draft judgment according to the Code.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to sentence according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，江西按察使黃翰言：「民間無籍之徒，好興詞論，輒令老幼殘疾男婦誣告平人，必更議涉虛加罰乃可。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, Regional Inspector Huang Han of Jiangxi said: "Among the people are unrestrained men who like to stir up lawsuits, habitually making the old, the young, the disabled, men, and women falsely accuse innocent persons; only after further review and a penalty for groundless accusation can it be settled."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande, Regional Inspector Huang Han of Jiangxi reported: "Idle troublemakers like to stir up lawsuits, often making the elderly, children, the disabled, men, or women bring false charges against innocent people; only after further review and a penalty for groundless accusation can the matter be settled.

sentences.zh: 遂定老幼殘疾男婦誣告人罰鈔贖罪例。

translations.literal: ] Thereupon a precedent was fixed imposing a fine in paper money for redeeming the crime when the old, young, disabled, men, or women falsely accused others.
translations.idiomatic: A precedent was then set: when the elderly, young, disabled, men, or women falsely accused others, they paid a paper-money fine to redeem the offense.

sentences.zh: 其後孝宗時，南京有犯誣告十人以上，例發口外為民。

translations.literal: Later, in the time of Emperor Xiaozong, at Nanjing one who falsely accused more than ten persons, by precedent, was banished beyond the passes to become a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Xiaozong, at Nanjing anyone who falsely accused more than ten people was, by precedent, banished beyond the frontier passes to live as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 而年逾七十，律應收贖者，更著令，凡年七十以上、十五以下及廢疾者，依律論斷。
