translations.literal: Yet if over seventy years of age, when the Code provides that ransom should be accepted, a further statute was issued: for all those seventy years old and above, fifteen and below, and the disabled or infirm, judgment would follow the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for those over seventy whom the Code allowed to ransom their punishment, a further order was issued: anyone seventy or older, fifteen or younger, or disabled would be judged according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 例應充軍暿愰哨、口外為民者，仍依律發遣。

translations.literal: Those by precedent subject to military exile at frontier sentry posts or banishment beyond the passes as commoners would still be dispatched according to the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Those who by precedent should be sent to military exile at distant frontier sentry posts or banished beyond the passes as commoners were still dispatched according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 若年八十以上及篤疾有犯應永戍者，以子孫發遣，應充軍以下者免之。

translations.literal: If eighty years old and above or gravely ill and guilty of what should be lifelong exile, their descendants would be sent; for what should be military exile or below, they were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: If offenders were eighty or older or gravely ill and liable to lifelong exile, their descendants were sent in their place; for punishments of military exile or less, they were exempted.

sentences.zh: 初制，凡官吏人等犯枉法贓者，不分南北，俱發北方邊衛充軍。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, whenever officials and others committed the crime of illegal bribes, without distinction between south and north, all were sent to northern frontier guards for military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original rule, any official or other person guilty of illegal bribery, north or south alike, was sent to northern frontier garrisons for military exile.

sentences.zh: 正統五年，行在三法司言：「洪武定律時，鈔貴物賤，所以枉法贓至百二十貫者，免絞充軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, the three judicial offices at the mobile court said: "When Hongwu fixed the Code, paper money was valuable and goods cheap, so illegal bribes reaching one hundred twenty strings were exempted from strangulation and sent instead to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, the three judicial offices at the mobile court reported: "When Hongwu enacted the Code, paper money was valuable and goods cheap, so illegal bribes of one hundred twenty strings or more were spared strangulation and sent to military exile instead.

sentences.zh: 今鈔賤物貴，若以物估鈔至百二十貫枉法贓俱發充軍，輕重失倫矣。

translations.literal: Now paper money is cheap and goods dear; if goods are valued in paper money and illegal bribes reaching one hundred twenty strings all go to military exile, severity would be inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Now paper money is cheap and goods dear; if bribes valued at one hundred twenty strings in paper money all led to military exile, the punishment would no longer fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 今後文職官吏人等，受枉法贓比律該絞者，估鈔八百貫之上，俱發北方邊衛充軍。

translations.literal: Henceforth, for civil officials and others who accept illegal bribes such that by the Code they merit strangulation, if valued at more than eight hundred strings in paper money, all are sent to northern frontier guards for military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, civil officials and others who took illegal bribes warranting strangulation under the Code, if the amount exceeded eight hundred strings in paper money, were all sent to northern frontier garrisons for military exile.

sentences.zh: 其受贓不及前數者，視見行例發落。」

translations.literal: Those whose bribes do not reach the former amount are dealt with according to current precedents."
translations.idiomatic: Those whose bribes fell short of that amount were punished under current precedents.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: ] The order was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，大理寺言：「律載竊盜初犯刺右臂，再犯刺左臂，三犯絞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Court of Judicial Review said: "The Code provides that for theft on the first offense the right arm is tattooed, on the second offense the left arm, and on the third offense strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the Court of Judicial Review reported: "The Code states that a first theft offense is marked by tattooing the right arm, a second by tattooing the left, and a third by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 今竊盜遇赦再犯者，鹹坐以初犯，或仍刺右臂，或不刺。

translations.literal: Now when thieves who have encountered amnesty reoffend, all are treated as on the first offense, or the right arm is tattooed again, or no tattooing is done.
translations.idiomatic: Now when thieves who had been pardoned reoffended, all were treated as first offenders, or the right arm was tattooed again, or no tattoo was applied at all.

sentences.zh: 請定為例。」

translations.literal: Request that this be fixed as a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that this be established as a precedent.

sentences.zh: 章下三法司議，刺右遇赦再犯者刺左，刺左遇赦又犯者不刺，立案。

translations.literal: ] The memorial was sent down for deliberation by the three judicial offices: those tattooed on the right who reoffend after amnesty are tattooed on the left; those tattooed on the left who reoffend again after amnesty are not tattooed, and this was established as a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the three judicial offices for deliberation: those tattooed on the right who reoffended after amnesty were tattooed on the left; those tattooed on the left who offended again after amnesty were not tattooed—and this was made precedent.

sentences.zh: 赦後三犯者絞。」

translations.literal: Those who offend three times after amnesty are strangled."
translations.idiomatic: A third offense after amnesty was punished by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「竊盜已刺，遇赦再犯者依常例擬，不論赦，仍通具前後所犯以聞。」

translations.literal: ] The emperor said: "Thieves already tattooed who reoffend after amnesty are to be drafted according to the regular articles, amnesty not considered; still fully report prior and subsequent offenses together."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Thieves already tattooed who reoffend after amnesty are to be sentenced under the regular articles, amnesty aside; still report all prior and subsequent offenses together.

sentences.zh: 後憲宗時，都御史李秉援舊例奏革。

translations.literal: ] Later in the time of Emperor Xianzong, Censor-in-Chief Li Bing cited the old precedent and memorialized to repeal it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Xianzong, Censor-in-Chief Li Bing cited the old precedent and memorialized for its repeal.

sentences.zh: 既而南京盜王阿童五犯皆遇赦免。

translations.literal: Soon after, the Nanjing thief Wang Atong committed five offenses and each time was freed by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, a Nanjing thief named Wang Atong committed five offenses and was freed by amnesty each time.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，詔仍以赦前後三犯為令。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he decreed that the rule of three offenses before and after amnesty should again stand.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he decreed that the rule of three offenses before and after amnesty should stand again.

sentences.zh: 至神宗時，復議奏請改遣云。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Shenzong, deliberation again memorialized requesting change in dispatch, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of Emperor Shenzong, officials again deliberated and memorialized to change how such offenders were punished.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以知縣陳敏政言，民以後妻所攜前夫之女為子婦，及以所攜前夫之子為婿者，並依同父異母姊妹律，減等科斷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, because Magistrate Chen Minzheng spoke, when commoners take a stepdaughter brought by a wife from a prior marriage as their son's wife, or take a stepson from a prior marriage as a son-in-law, all are sentenced with reduced grades according to the statute on half-sisters sharing the same father.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, on Magistrate Chen Minzheng's report, when commoners took a stepdaughter from a wife's prior marriage as a daughter-in-law, or a stepson from that marriage as a son-in-law, both were sentenced with reduced severity under the statute on half-sisters by the same father.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，遼東巡撫滕照言：「《大明律》乃一代定法，而決斷武臣，獨舍律用例，武臣益縱蕩不檢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Grand Coordinator Teng Zhao of Liaodong said: "The Great Ming Code is the fixed law of a generation, yet in deciding cases of military officers the Code alone is set aside and precedents used, so military officers grow ever more unrestrained and unregulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua, Grand Coordinator Teng Zhao of Liaodong said: "The Great Ming Code is the fixed law of the dynasty, yet in judging military officers the Code is set aside and precedents used instead, so military officers grow ever more unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 請一切用律。」

translations.literal: Request that the Code be used in all cases."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Code be applied in all cases.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: ] An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 武臣被黜降者，騰口謗訕，有司畏事，復奏革其令。

translations.literal: Military officers who were removed or demoted slandered by spreading rumors; the officials, fearing trouble, again memorialized to repeal the order.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed or demoted military officers spread slander; fearing trouble, officials memorialized again to repeal the order.

sentences.zh: 十九年定，竊盜三犯罪例。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year it was fixed: precedent on three-time theft offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year a precedent on three-time theft offenses was established.

sentences.zh: 法司以「南京有三犯竊盜，計贓滿百貫者犯，當絞斬。

translations.literal: The judicial offices said: "In Nanjing there is a three-time thief whose accumulated stolen goods reach one hundred strings, and the offense merits decapitation by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices reported: "In Nanjing there is a three-time thief whose stolen goods total one hundred strings; the offense merits decapitation by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 罪雖雜犯，其情頗重。」

translations.literal: Although the crime is among miscellaneous offenses, the circumstances are rather grave."
translations.idiomatic: Although the offense is a miscellaneous crime, the circumstances are grave.

sentences.zh: 三犯前罪，即累惡不悛之人，難準常例。

translations.literal: ] One who has prior offenses on the third conviction is a person who accumulates wickedness without reform and cannot be measured by ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A third conviction with prior offenses marks someone who accumulates wickedness without reform and cannot be judged by ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 其不滿貫犯，徒流以下罪者，雖至三犯，原情實輕，宜特依常例治之。」

translations.literal: Those who do not reach one hundred strings and whose offense is penal servitude, exile, or below—even on the third conviction, the original circumstances are truly light, and they should specially be punished according to ordinary precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Those whose stolen goods fall short of one hundred strings and whose offenses are penal servitude, exile, or less—even on a third conviction, the original circumstances are truly light and should be punished under ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 議上，報允。

translations.literal: ] The deliberation was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年，太常少卿李東陽言：「五刑最輕者笞杖，然杖有分寸，數有多寡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi, Vice Minister of Rites Li Dongyang said: "Of the five punishments, the lightest are beating with the rod or stick; yet rods and sticks have definite dimensions and strokes have definite number.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi, Vice Minister of Rites Li Dongyang said: "Of the five punishments, the lightest are beating with rod or stick—yet rods and sticks have fixed dimensions and strokes have fixed counts.

sentences.zh: 今在外諸司，笞杖之罪往往致死。

translations.literal: Now in the various offices outside the capital, rod-and-stick punishments often cause death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in offices outside the capital, rod-and-stick punishments often kill the offender.

sentences.zh: 縱令事覺，不過以因公還職。

translations.literal: Even if the matter comes to light, it amounts to no more than restoration to office on grounds of public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Even when discovered, the official is merely restored to office on grounds of acting in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 以極輕之刑，置之不可復生之地，多者數十，甚者數百，積骸滿獄，流血塗地，可為傷心。

translations.literal: With the lightest punishment, men are placed beyond recovery—sometimes numbering in the tens, sometimes in the hundreds; corpses fill the prisons and blood soaks the ground—this is heartbreaking.
translations.idiomatic: With the lightest punishments, men are sent to their deaths—sometimes dozens, sometimes hundreds; corpses fill the prisons and blood soaks the ground. It is heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 律故勘平人者抵命，刑具非法者除名，偶不出此，便謂之公。

translations.literal: The Code provides that those who deliberately examine and kill innocent persons pay with their lives, and those who use unlawful instruments of punishment are removed from office; if one happens not to fall within these, it is called public service.
translations.idiomatic: The Code requires that those who deliberately torture innocent people to death pay with their lives, and those who use unlawful instruments of punishment are dismissed—yet if a case falls outside these rules, it is called acting in the public interest.

sentences.zh: 一以公名，雖多無害。

translations.literal: Once labeled public service, even many deaths do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Once labeled as public service, even many deaths bring no harm to the official.

sentences.zh: 此則情重而律輕者，不可以不議也。

translations.literal: Here feeling is grave while the Code is light—this cannot go undebated.
translations.idiomatic: Here the circumstances are grave while the Code is lenient—this cannot go undebated.

sentences.zh: 請凡考訊輕罪即時致死，累二十或三十人以上，本律外，仍議行降調，或病死不實者，並治其醫。」

translations.literal: Request that wherever examination of minor crimes causes immediate death, accumulating twenty or thirty persons or more, beyond the original statute, demotion or transfer still be deliberated; and where death by illness was falsely reported, the physician too be punished."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that whenever interrogation for minor offenses causes immediate death, and the victims number twenty or thirty or more, officials beyond the original statute still face demotion or transfer; and where death by illness was falsely claimed, the physician be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 乃下所司議處。

translations.literal: ] It was then sent down to the offices for deliberation and disposition.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年，時有以手足毆人傷重，延至辜限外死者，部擬鬥毆殺人論絞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing, at that time there were cases in which injury by beating with hands or feet was grave and the person died after the statutory period of suspense for wounds had passed; the ministry drafted judgment as killing in affray by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing, when someone beat another with hands or feet, inflicted grave injury, and the victim died after the statutory wound-suspense period had passed, the ministry drafted a sentence of strangulation for killing in affray.

sentences.zh: 大理寺執嘉靖四年例，謂當以毆傷論笞。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review held to the precedent of the fourth year of Jiajing, saying it should be judged as beating causing injury with rod punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review cited the precedent of Jiajing year four, arguing that it should be punished as beating causing injury, with rod strokes only.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「律定辜限，而《問刑條例》又謂鬥毆殺人、情實事實者，雖延至限外，仍擬死罪，奏請定奪。

translations.literal: The ministry officials said: "The Code fixes the period of suspense, but the Criminal Code Precedents also say that in killing in affray where the facts and feeling are real, even if death extends beyond the period, capital punishment is still drafted for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials said: "The Code sets a wound-suspense period, but the Criminal Code Precedents also state that in killing during affray, when the facts and intent are clear, even if death occurs after the period expires, capital punishment is still drafted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 臣部擬上，每奉宸斷，多發充軍，蓋雖不執前科，亦僅末減之耳。

translations.literal: When our ministry submits drafts, we often receive imperial verdicts mostly sending to military exile—for though prior penalties are not applied, it is only a slight reduction at the end.
translations.idiomatic: When our ministry submits such cases, imperial verdicts usually send the offender to military exile—for though the death penalty is not applied, this is only a slight reduction at the end.

sentences.zh: 毆傷情實至限外死，即以笞斷，是乃僥倖兇人也。

translations.literal: Beating causing injury with real circumstances leading to death beyond the period and then judged only with rod punishment—this indulges violent men by luck.
translations.idiomatic: To punish beating that in fact causes death beyond the suspense period with only rod strokes is to let violent men escape by luck.

sentences.zh: 且如以兇器傷人，雖平復，例亦充軍，豈有實毆人致死，偶死限外，遂不當一兇器傷人之罪乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, wounding with a deadly weapon, even if healing is complete, by precedent still brings military exile—how can real beating causing death, if death happens accidentally outside the period, not merit even the crime of wounding with a deadly weapon?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wounding with a deadly weapon, even if the victim recovers, still brings military exile by precedent—how can someone who in fact beats another to death, if death happens only by chance after the period, deserve less than the crime of wounding with a deadly weapon?

sentences.zh: 矧四年例已報罷，請諭中外仍如《條例》便。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the precedent of the fourth year has already been reported repealed; please instruct inside and outside to follow the Precedents as before."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the year-four precedent has already been repealed; please instruct officials throughout the realm to follow the Precedents as before.

sentences.zh: 詔如部議。

translations.literal: ] An edict followed the ministry's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the ministry's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 自後有犯辜限外人命者，俱遵律例議擬，奏請定奪。

translations.literal: Thereafter, those guilty of taking human life outside the period of suspense all followed the Code and precedents in deliberation and memorialized for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, all cases of homicide outside the wound-suspense period were deliberated under the Code and precedents and memorialized for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，大理少卿王諍言：「問刑官每違背律例，獨任意見。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Zheng said: "Judges in criminal cases often violate the Code and precedents and act solely on private opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longqing, Vice Minister Wang Zheng of the Court of Judicial Review said: "Criminal judges often violate the Code and precedents and act on private opinion alone.

sentences.zh: 如律文所謂『凡奉制書，有所施行而違者杖一百』，本指制誥而言。

translations.literal: As the Code text says, 'Whoever fails to carry out what is ordered in an imperial command document shall be beaten one hundred strokes'—this originally referred to edicts of command.
translations.idiomatic: As the Code says, 'Whoever disobeys an imperial command document in its execution shall receive one hundred strokes'—this originally referred to formal imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 今則操軍違限，守備官軍不入直，開場賭博，概用此例。

translations.literal: Now troops who exceed time limits, garrison officers and soldiers who fail to enter duty, and opening grounds for gambling—all use this article indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Now soldiers who miss drill deadlines, garrison officers who fail to report for duty, and those who run gambling dens—all are punished under this article indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 律文犯奸條下，所謂『買休賣休、和娶人妻者』，本指用財買求其妻，又使之休賣其妻，而因以娶之者言也。

translations.literal: Under the adultery article in the Code, what is called 'buying rest, selling rest, and peacefully taking another's wife' originally meant using wealth to buy her from her husband, also making him sell and rest his wife, and thereby marrying her.
translations.idiomatic: Under the adultery article, what is called 'buying rest, selling rest, and peacefully taking another man's wife' originally meant using money to buy a man's consent, making him divorce and sell his wife, and then marrying her oneself.

sentences.zh: 故律應離異歸宗，財禮入官。

translations.literal: Therefore the Code required separation and return to the ancestral lineage, and betrothal wealth went to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Code required divorce and return to her original lineage, and betrothal gifts were forfeited to the state.

sentences.zh: 至若夫婦不合者，律應離異；

translations.literal: Where husband and wife were incompatible, the Code required separation;
translations.idiomatic: Where husband and wife were incompatible, the Code required divorce;

sentences.zh: 婦人犯奸者，律從嫁賣；

translations.literal: where a woman committed adultery, the Code allowed her to be married off or sold;
translations.idiomatic: where a woman committed adultery, the Code allowed her to be remarried or sold;

sentences.zh: 則後夫憑媒用財娶以為妻者，原非姦情，律所不禁。

translations.literal: then when a later husband through a matchmaker used wealth to take her as wife, there was originally no adulterous intent, and the Code did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: when a later husband took her through a matchmaker with payment, there was originally no adulterous intent, and the Code did not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 今則概引買休、賣休、和娶之律矣。

translations.literal: Now the statutes on buying rest, selling rest, and peaceful taking are cited indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Now the statutes on buying rest, selling rest, and peaceful taking are cited indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 所謂『不應得為而為者，笞四十，重者杖八十』。

translations.literal: What is called 'doing what should not be done—beat forty strokes, in grave cases beat eighty.'
translations.idiomatic: What is called 'doing what ought not to be done—forty strokes of the rod; in grave cases, eighty strokes of the stick.'

sentences.zh: 蓋謂律文該載不盡者，方用此律也。

translations.literal: This meant only where the Code text did not fully cover the case should this statute be used.
translations.idiomatic: This statute was meant only where the Code did not fully cover the offense.

sentences.zh: 若所犯明有正條，自當依本條科斷。

translations.literal: If the offense clearly had a proper article, judgment should follow that article.
translations.idiomatic: If the offense clearly fell under a specific article, judgment should follow that article.

sentences.zh: 今所犯毆人成傷，罪宜笞，而議罪者則曰『除毆人成傷，律輕不坐外，合依不應得為而為之事理，重者律杖八十』。

translations.literal: Now one who beats another causing injury should be punished with rods, yet the judge says: 'Apart from beating causing injury, where the statute is light and no punishment sits, combine with doing what should not be done in principle—in grave cases beat eighty by statute.'
translations.idiomatic: Today someone who beats another and causes injury should receive rod punishment, yet the judge says: 'Apart from the light offense of beating causing injury, which carries no punishment, apply the principle of doing what ought not to be done—in grave cases, eighty strokes by statute.'

sentences.zh: 夫既除毆人輕罪不坐，則無罪可坐矣。

translations.literal: Having already excluded the light offense of beating and left nothing punishable, there is no crime on which to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Having already excluded the light offense of beating, there is no crime left to punish.

sentences.zh: 而又坐以『不應得為』，臣誠不知其所謂。」

translations.literal: Yet again punish under 'doing what should not be done'—your servant truly does not understand what this means."
translations.idiomatic: Yet they punish under 'doing what ought not to be done'—I truly do not understand what this means.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書毛愷力爭之，廷臣皆是諍議。

translations.literal: ] Minister of Punishments Mao Kai argued forcefully; court officials all approved Zheng's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Mao Kai argued forcefully against it, but court officials all sided with Wang Zheng's position.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「買休、賣休，本屬奸條，今後有犯，非系姦情者，不得引用。

translations.literal: The rescript said: "Buying rest and selling rest originally belong to the adultery articles; hereafter when there is an offense, if it does not involve adulterous intent, this may not be cited.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "Buying rest and selling rest belong to the adultery articles; hereafter, when there is an offense, if adulterous intent is not involved, these statutes may not be cited.

sentences.zh: 他如故。」

translations.literal: Other matters remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Other matters remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，左都御史吳時來申明律例六條：

translations.literal: During the Wanli period, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai clarified six articles of the Code and precedents:
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai clarified six points on the Code and precedents:

sentences.zh: 一、律稱庶人之家不許存養奴婢。

translations.literal: First, the Code says that commoners' households may not keep and rear slave girls and boys.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Code states that commoners' households may not keep and rear slaves.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂功臣家方給賞奴婢，庶民當自服勤勞，故不得存養。

translations.literal: This means only meritorious officials' households were granted reward of slaves; commoners should serve by their own labor, hence may not keep them.
translations.idiomatic: This means only meritorious officials' households were granted slaves as reward; commoners should labor for themselves, and therefore may not keep them.

sentences.zh: 有犯者皆稱僱工人，初未言及縉紳之家也。

translations.literal: Offenders all called them hired laborers; at first this did not speak of gentry and official households.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders all called them hired laborers; at first the rule did not address gentry and official households.

sentences.zh: 縉紳之家，存養奴婢，勢所不免。

translations.literal: Gentry and official households keeping slave girls and boys was a circumstance that could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: For gentry and official households, keeping slaves was unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 合令法司酌議，無論官民之家，立券用值、工作有年限者，以僱工人論；

translations.literal: Let the judicial offices deliberate: for official and common households alike, where there is a contract and payment of value and labor for a fixed term, treat as hired laborer;
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices should deliberate: for official and common households alike, where there is a written contract, payment of wages, and labor for a fixed term, treat the person as a hired laborer;

sentences.zh: 受值微少、工作計日月者，以凡人論。

translations.literal: those who receive little value and whose labor is counted by day and month, treat as ordinary persons.
translations.idiomatic: those who receive little payment and whose work is counted by the day or month, treat as ordinary persons.

sentences.zh: 若財買十五以下、恩養日久、十六以上、配有室家者，視同子孫論。

translations.literal: If purchased below age fifteen, long nurtured by kindness, and above sixteen with spouse and household assigned, treat like descendants.
translations.idiomatic: If purchased before age fifteen, long nurtured with kindness, and after sixteen given a spouse and household, treat like descendants.

sentences.zh: 或恩養未久，不曾配合者，庶人之家，仍以僱工人論；

translations.literal: Or if kindness-nurtured not long and not yet given a spouse—in commoners' households still treat as hired laborer;
translations.idiomatic: Or if nurtured for only a short time and not yet given a spouse—in commoners' households still treat as hired laborer;

sentences.zh: 縉紳之家，視奴婢律論。

translations.literal: in gentry and official households, treat according to the slave statute.
translations.idiomatic: in gentry and official households, treat according to the slave statute.

sentences.zh: 一、律稱偽造諸衙門印信者斬。

translations.literal: First, the Code says that forging seals of the various yamen merits decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Code states that forging seals of government offices merits decapitation.

sentences.zh: 惟銅鐵私鑄者，故斬。

translations.literal: Only private casting in copper or iron therefore merits decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Only privately cast copper or iron seals therefore merit decapitation.

sentences.zh: 若篆文雖印，形質非印者，不可謂之偽造，故例又立描摸充軍之條。

translations.literal: If the seal script is impressed but the form is not a true seal, it cannot be called forgery; therefore precedents also established an article on tracing and imitating, punished with military exile.
translations.idiomatic: If seal characters are impressed but the object is not a true seal, it cannot be called forgery; therefore precedents also established an article on tracing and imitation, punished with military exile.

sentences.zh: 以後偽造印信人犯，如系木石泥蠟之類，止引描摸之例，若再犯擬斬。

translations.literal: Hereafter, offenders in forging seals—if of wood, stone, clay, wax, and the like—cite only the tracing precedent; if they reoffend, draft decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, offenders who forge seals of wood, stone, clay, wax, and the like should be sentenced only under the tracing precedent; on a second offense, draft decapitation.

sentences.zh: 偽造行使止一次、而贓不滿徒者，亦準竊盜論。

translations.literal: Forging and use only once, and stolen goods not reaching penal servitude, also judge like theft.
translations.idiomatic: If forgery was used only once and the illicit gain does not reach the threshold for penal servitude, judge as theft.

sentences.zh: 如再犯引例，三犯引律。

translations.literal: On a second offense cite the precedent; on a third offense cite the Code.
translations.idiomatic: On a second offense apply the precedent; on a third, apply the Code.

sentences.zh: 一、律稱竊盜三犯者絞，以曾經刺字為坐。

translations.literal: First, the Code says that a thief on a third offense is strangled, the punishment being based on having formerly been tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Code states that a thief who commits a third offense is sentenced to strangulation, because prior tattooing establishes the count.

sentences.zh: 但贓有多寡，即擬有輕重。

translations.literal: Yet according to whether the stolen goods are many or few, the draft sentence has lightness or heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, the amount stolen still determines whether the proposed sentence is lighter or heavier.

sentences.zh: 以後凡遇竊盜，三犯俱在赦前、俱在赦後者，依律論絞。

translations.literal: Hereafter, whenever encountering thieves, if all three offenses are before an amnesty or all after an amnesty, judge strangulation according to the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, in theft cases where all three offenses fall either entirely before or entirely after an amnesty, sentence strangulation according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 或赦前後所犯並計三次者，皆得奏請定奪。

translations.literal: Or if offenses before and after an amnesty are together counted as three times, all may memorialize requesting imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: When offenses before and after an amnesty are combined to reach three convictions, the case may be memorialized for the throne's decision.

sentences.zh: 錄官附入矜疑辨問疏內，並與改遣。

translations.literal: Record the officials and attach them within the memorial on leniency and doubtful cases, and together grant commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Record such cases in the memorial on leniency and doubtful sentencing, and commute the punishment.

sentences.zh: 一、強盜肆行劫殺，按贓擬闢，決不待時。

translations.literal: First, robbers who rampantly rob and kill are, according to stolen goods, drafted for immediate execution; the sentence is not held for a season.
translations.idiomatic: First, robbers who murder in the course of brigandage are, according to the loot, sentenced to immediate execution without seasonal delay.

sentences.zh: 但其中豈無羅織讎扳，妄收抵罪者？

translations.literal: But among them, are there not those framed by entanglement and dragged in by vendetta, wrongly seized to atone for the crime?
translations.idiomatic: Yet among these cases, surely some are framed or dragged in by private vengeance—innocent men wrongly convicted.

sentences.zh: 以後務加參詳。

translations.literal: Hereafter strive to add thorough deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter such cases must be examined with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 或贓證未明，遽難懸斷者，俱擬秋後斬。

translations.literal: Or where evidence of stolen goods is unclear and hasty judgment is difficult, all are drafted for autumn execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the evidence of loot is unclear and a hasty verdict is impossible, all alike are to be sentenced to execution after autumn.

sentences.zh: 一、律稱同謀共毆人，以致命傷重，下手者論絞，原謀餘人各得其罪。

translations.literal: First, the Code says that those who conspire together to beat a person, with fatal serious wound as the weight—whoever struck is judged strangulation; the original conspirators and the rest each receive their crime.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Code provides that when conspirators jointly beat someone and the injury proves fatal, the striker is sentenced to strangulation while the instigator and the others are punished according to their respective roles.

sentences.zh: 其有兩三人共毆一人，各成重傷，難定下手及系造謀主令之人，遇有在監禁斃者，即以論抵。

translations.literal: Where two or three jointly beat one person, each causing serious injury, and it is hard to fix who struck and who was the instigator who commanded—if one dies in prison while confined, that one is used to balance the sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When two or three beat one man and each inflicts serious injury, so that neither the striker nor the instigator can be identified—if one dies in custody, that person satisfies the capital charge.

sentences.zh: 今恤刑官遇有在家病故，且在數年之後者，即將見監下手之人擬從矜宥。

translations.literal: Now the officials for merciful punishment, when they encounter one who died of illness at home years afterward, immediately draft the striker still in prison for lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Today, mercy-review officials often treat a beating victim who died at home years later as grounds to draft leniency for the striker still in prison.

sentences.zh: 是以病亡之軀，而抵毆死之命，殊屬縱濫。

translations.literal: Thus using a body that died of illness to balance a life taken by beating is excessively lax.
translations.idiomatic: To settle a beating death with someone who merely died of illness is glaringly lenient.

sentences.zh: 以後毋得一概準抵。

translations.literal: Hereafter do not uniformly permit balancing.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter this substitution must not be applied as a blanket rule.

sentences.zh: 一、在京惡逆與強盜真犯，雖停刑之年，亦不時處決。

translations.literal: First, in the capital, revolt and true robbery offenders, even in years when executions are suspended, are still executed without seasonal delay.
translations.idiomatic: First, in the capital, offenders guilty of rebellion or true robbery are executed immediately even in years when executions are normally suspended.

sentences.zh: 乃兇惡至於殺父，即時淩遲，猶有餘憾。

translations.literal: Yet when depravity reaches killing one's father, even immediate dismemberment still leaves regret.
translations.idiomatic: When depravity reaches parricide, even immediate slicing execution still feels insufficient.

sentences.zh: 而在外此類反得遷延歲月，以故事當類奏，無單奏例耳。

translations.literal: Yet outside the capital such cases can drag on for months and years, because by precedent they should be class-memorialized, without a single-memorial precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the provinces such cases may drag on for years, because precedent requires batched memorials and provides no rule for individual presentation.

sentences.zh: 夫單奏，急詞也；

translations.literal: A single memorial is urgent language;
translations.idiomatic: A single memorial is the language of urgency;

sentences.zh: 類奏，緩詞也。

translations.literal: a class memorial is slow language.
translations.idiomatic: a batched memorial is the language of delay.

sentences.zh: 如此獄在外數年，使其瘐死，將何以快神人之憤哉！

translations.literal: If such a case lingers outside for years and lets the prisoner waste away and die, how can the wrath of gods and men be satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: If such cases linger in the provinces for years until the prisoner wastes away in jail, how can the wrath of heaven and humanity ever be appeased!

sentences.zh: 今後在外，凡有此者，御史單詳到院，院寺單奏，決單一到，即時處決。

translations.literal: Hereafter outside, for all such cases the censor reports singly to the court, the court and ministry memorialize singly; when the execution order arrives singly, execute immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, in the provinces, for all such cases the censor shall report directly to the judicial court, and the court and ministry shall present an individual memorial; as soon as the execution order arrives, carry out the sentence at once.

sentences.zh: 其死者下府州縣戮其屍。

translations.literal: If already dead, the prefecture and counties below shall humiliate the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: If the offender has already died, the local prefecture and counties shall expose and mutilate the corpse.

sentences.zh: 庶典刑得正。

translations.literal: Thus the canonical punishment may be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus canonical punishment may be properly upheld.

sentences.zh: 旨下部寺酌議，俱從之。

translations.literal: The imperial order went to the ministry and court for deliberation; all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order directed the ministry and court to deliberate; all recommendations were approved.

sentences.zh: 惟偽造印文者，不問何物成造，皆斬。

translations.literal: Only for forgers of seal script—regardless of what material was used to make them—all are decapitated.
translations.idiomatic: Only for forging seal impressions: regardless of the material, all offenders are sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Report approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 贖刑本《虞書》，《呂刑》有大辟之贖，後世皆重言之。

translations.literal: Ransom punishment originates in the "Canon of Shun"; the "Punishments of Lü" has ransom for the great statute; later ages all spoke of it heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation by ransom originates in the Canon of Shun; the Punishments of Lü already allowed ransom even for capital crimes, and later dynasties all treated the practice as weighty.

sentences.zh: 至宋時，尤慎贖罪，非八議者不得與。

translations.literal: By the Song, ransom of crimes was especially cautious; those not in the Eight Deliberations could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, ransom was especially restricted: only those within the Eight Deliberations might participate.

sentences.zh: 明律頗嚴，凡朝廷有所矜恤、限於律而不得伸者，一寓之於贖例，所以濟法之太重也。

translations.literal: Ming law was quite strict; whatever the court wished to show mercy on but could not extend because limited by the Code—all was lodged in ransom precedents, thereby to relieve the law's excessive heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: Ming law was severe; whatever mercy the court wished to extend but could not under the Code was lodged entirely in ransom precedents, to soften punishments that would otherwise be too harsh.

sentences.zh: 又國家得時藉其入，以佐緩急。

translations.literal: Moreover the state could at times borrow its intake to assist in urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: The state, moreover, could draw on these payments in times of need.

sentences.zh: 而實邊、足儲、振荒、宮府頒給諸大費，往往取給於贓贖二者。

translations.literal: Yet in truth border defense, filling granaries, famine relief, palace and government distribution of major expenses—often supplies were drawn from stolen goods and ransom together.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, major expenses—frontier defense, filling granaries, famine relief, palace and government distributions—were often met from confiscated booty and ransom payments alike.

sentences.zh: 故贖法比歷代特詳。

translations.literal: Therefore ransom law was especially detailed compared with successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Ming ransom law was more elaborate than that of any earlier dynasty.

sentences.zh: 凡贖法有二，有律得收贖者，有例得納贖者。

translations.literal: In all, ransom law had two kinds: those who by the Code might have ransom received, and those who by precedent might pay ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Ransom took two forms: statutory redemption allowed by the Code, and pecuniary commutation allowed by precedent.

sentences.zh: 律贖無敢損益，而納贖之例則因時權宜，先後互異，其端實開於太祖云。

translations.literal: Code ransom none dared to diminish or increase; but the precedents for paying ransom shifted with timely expediency, early and late mutually differing—the origin truly opened with the founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory ransom rates were inviolable, but precedents for paying ransom shifted with the times and often contradicted one another—a practice that began under the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 律凡文武官以公事犯笞罪者，官照等收贖錢，吏每季類決之，各還職役，不附過。

translations.literal: The Code: whenever civil and military officials commit cane offenses on public business, officials redeem money according to rank, clerks are sentenced by category each quarter, each returns to office and duty, no demerit attached.
translations.idiomatic: The Code provided that when civil or military officials incurred cane punishments for public-service offenses, officials paid ransom according to rank, while clerks were sentenced in batches each quarter; all returned to duty without a recorded demerit.

sentences.zh: 杖以上記所犯罪名，每歲類送吏、兵二部，候九年滿考，通記所犯次數黜陟之。

translations.literal: For rod and above the crime name was recorded; each year they were sent in categories to the Ministries of Personnel and War; awaiting nine years for full review, the total of offenses was recorded for promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Rod punishments and above were recorded by name of offense and reported yearly to the Ministries of Personnel and War; at the nine-year review, the cumulative count governed promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 吏典亦備銓選降敘。

translations.literal: Clerks and registry officers likewise were subject to selection, reduction, and demotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and registry officers likewise faced reduction in selection and rank.

sentences.zh: 至於私罪，其文官及吏典犯笞四十以下者，附過還職而不贖，笞五十者調用。

translations.literal: As for private crimes—where civil officials and registry officers commit forty cane-blows or below, demerit was attached and they returned to office without ransom; fifty cane-blows brought transfer.
translations.idiomatic: For private offenses: civil officials and clerks who incurred up to forty blows of the cane kept their posts with a recorded demerit and no ransom; at fifty blows they were transferred.

sentences.zh: 軍官杖以上皆的決。

translations.literal: Military officers for rod and above were all executed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: For military officers, rod punishment and above were always inflicted in person.

sentences.zh: 文官及吏杖罪，並罷職不敘，至嚴也。

translations.literal: Civil officials and clerics with rod crimes—all dismissed from office and not reappointed; extremely strict.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials and clerks who incurred the rod were dismissed and never reappointed—an extremely strict rule.

sentences.zh: 然自洪武中年已三下令，準贖及雜犯死罪以下矣。

translations.literal: Yet from the middle years of Hongwu there were already three orders permitting ransom, down to miscellaneous crimes and death below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the middle Hongwu reign three orders had already authorized ransom even for miscellaneous offenses down to lesser capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 三十年，命部院議定贖罪事例，凡內外官吏，犯笞杖者記過，徒流遷徙者俸贖之，三犯罪之如律。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, ordered the ministries and courts to deliberate and fix ransom-crime precedents: all officials inside and outside who committed cane or rod had demerits recorded; penal servitude, exile, and banishment were ransomed with salary; three offenses were punished as the Code.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, ministries and courts were ordered to set ransom precedents: officials who incurred cane or rod punishments received recorded demerits; penal servitude, exile, and banishment could be commuted by salary payment; a third offense was punished according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 自是律與例互有異同。

translations.literal: From this the Code and precedents mutually had differences and samenesses.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the Code and precedents often diverged.

sentences.zh: 及頒行《大明律》，御製序：「雜犯死罪、徒流、遷徙等刑，悉視今定贖罪條例科斷。」

translations.literal: When the Great Ming Code was promulgated, the imperial preface said: "Miscellaneous death crimes, penal servitude, exile, banishment, and other punishments—all look to the now-fixed ransom-crime regulations for judgment."
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Ming Code was promulgated, the imperial preface declared: "Miscellaneous capital crimes, penal servitude, exile, banishment, and similar punishments shall all be adjudicated under the newly fixed ransom regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是例遂輔律而行。

translations.literal: ] Thus precedents then assisted the Code in operation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus precedents came to supplement the Code in practice.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初即位，諭都察院言：「輸罰工作之令行，有財者悉倖免，宜一論如律。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong first took the throne, he instructed the Censorate: "The order to pay fines and perform labor is in force; those with wealth all luckily escape; it is fitting to judge all alike according to the Code."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong first ascended the throne, he told the Censorate: "The rule allowing fine payment and labor service lets the wealthy escape punishment entirely; all offenders should be sentenced according to the Code alone.

sentences.zh: 久之，其法復弛。

translations.literal: ] After long time, that law again grew lax.
translations.idiomatic: In time the rule lapsed again.

sentences.zh: 正統間，侍講劉球言：「輸罪非古，自公罪許贖外，宜悉依律。」

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period, Lecturer Liu Qiu said: "Paying for crimes is not ancient; apart from permitting ransom for public crimes, all should follow the Code."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, Lecturer Liu Qiu argued: "Pecuniary commutation is unorthodox; apart from statutory ransom for public offenses, all should follow the Code.

sentences.zh: 時不能從。

translations.literal: ] At the time they could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The court could not accept this at the time.

sentences.zh: 其後循太祖之例，益推廣之。

translations.literal: Thereafter following the founding emperor's precedents, it was further extended.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, following the founding emperor's precedents, the system was expanded further.

sentences.zh: 凡官吏公私雜犯準徒以下，俱聽運炭納米等項贖罪。

translations.literal: All officials' public and private miscellaneous offenses down to penal servitude—all were permitted to ransom crimes by transporting charcoal, delivering rice, and such items.
translations.idiomatic: Officials guilty of public or private miscellaneous offenses down to penal servitude were allowed to commute punishment by hauling charcoal, delivering rice, and similar services.

sentences.zh: 其軍官軍人照例免徒流者，例贖亦如之矣。

translations.literal: Military officers and soldiers who by precedent were exempted from penal servitude and exile—precedent ransom was likewise applied to them.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers and soldiers already exempt from penal servitude and exile under precedent were granted the same commutation privileges.

sentences.zh: 贖罪之法，明初嘗納銅，成化間嘗納馬，後皆不行，不具載。

translations.literal: The law of ransoming crimes—early Ming once accepted copper; Chenghua period once accepted horses; later none were implemented, not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming once accepted copper ransom; the Chenghua reign once accepted horses; neither practice endured and neither is fully recorded here.

sentences.zh: 惟納鈔、納錢、納銀常並行焉，而以初制納鈔為本。

translations.literal: Only paying paper money, paying coin, and paying silver constantly ran in parallel, with the initial system's paying paper money as root.
translations.idiomatic: Only payment in paper notes, coin, and silver remained in constant parallel use, with the original paper-note system as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 故律贖者曰收贖律鈔，納贖者曰贖罪例鈔。

translations.literal: Therefore those who ransomed by the Code were called receiving statutory ransom paper; those who paid ransom were called ransom-crime precedent paper.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory redemption was called "Code ransom notes"; pecuniary commutation was called "precedent ransom notes."

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年，令除公罪依例紀錄收贖，及死罪情重者依律處治，其情輕者，斬罪八千貫，絞罪及榜例死罪六千貫，流徒杖笞納鈔有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle, an order: apart from public crimes recorded and ransomed by precedent, and grave death crimes punished according to the Code—for light circumstances, decapitation eight thousand strings, strangulation and beating-precedent death six thousand strings; exile, penal servitude, rod, and cane paid paper money with differences.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongle, an order provided that public offenses would be recorded and redeemed under precedent, and grave capital cases punished according to the Code; in lighter cases, decapitation required eight thousand strings of notes, strangulation and death by beating under precedent six thousand strings, with graded payments for exile, penal servitude, rod, and cane.

sentences.zh: 無力者發天壽山種樹。

translations.literal: Those without means were sent to plant trees at Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay were sent to plant trees on Tianshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年定，笞杖罪囚，每十贖鈔二十貫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande it was fixed: cane and rod offenders, for every ten blows ransom twenty strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande, a rule was set: for cane and rod offenses, every ten blows required twenty strings of paper notes in ransom.

sentences.zh: 徒流罪名，每徒一等折杖二十，三流並折杖百四十。

translations.literal: For penal servitude and exile crimes, each degree of servitude converted to twenty rod blows; all three exiles together converted to one hundred forty rod blows.
translations.idiomatic: For penal servitude and exile, each degree of servitude converted to twenty blows of the rod; all three degrees of exile together converted to one hundred forty blows.

sentences.zh: 其所罰鈔，悉如笞杖所定。

translations.literal: The paper money fined all followed what was fixed for cane and rod.
translations.idiomatic: The paper-note fines all followed the rates set for cane and rod offenses.

sentences.zh: 無力者發天壽山種樹；

translations.literal: Those without means were sent to plant trees at Tianshou Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay were sent to plant trees on Tianshou Mountain;

sentences.zh: 死罪終身；

translations.literal: death crimes for life;
translations.idiomatic: capital offenders for life;

sentences.zh: 徒流各按年限；

translations.literal: penal servitude and exile each according to term limits;
translations.idiomatic: penal servitude and exile according to the term of sentence;

sentences.zh: 杖，五百株；

translations.literal: rod, five hundred saplings;
translations.idiomatic: rod punishment, five hundred trees;

sentences.zh: 笞，一百株。

translations.literal: cane, one hundred saplings.
translations.idiomatic: cane punishment, one hundred trees.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，令問擬笞杖罪囚，有力者納鈔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, ordered that when drafting cane and rod offenders, those with means pay paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, an order provided that when sentencing cane and rod offenders, those with means might pay paper notes.

sentences.zh: 笞十，二百貫，每十以二百貫遞加，至笞五十為千貫。

translations.literal: Ten cane blows, two hundred strings; for every ten an increase of two hundred strings, up to fifty cane blows as one thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Ten blows of the cane: two hundred strings; each additional ten blows added two hundred strings, reaching one thousand strings at fifty blows.

sentences.zh: 杖六十，千八百貫，每十以三百貫遞加，至杖百為三千貫。

translations.literal: Sixty rod blows, one thousand eight hundred strings; for every ten an increase of three hundred strings, up to one hundred rod blows as three thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty blows of the rod: one thousand eight hundred strings; each additional ten blows added three hundred strings, reaching three thousand strings at one hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 其官吏贓物，亦視今例折鈔。

translations.literal: Officials' stolen goods likewise were converted to paper money according to present precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' illicit gains were likewise converted to paper notes under current precedents.

sentences.zh: 天順五年，令罪囚納鈔，每笞十，鈔二百貫，餘四笞，遞加百五十貫；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun, ordered offenders to pay paper money: for every ten cane blows, two hundred strings of notes; for the remaining four cane gradations, an increase of one hundred fifty strings each;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun, offenders were ordered to pay paper notes: every ten blows of the cane required two hundred strings; for each of the four remaining cane gradations, one hundred fifty strings were added;

sentences.zh: 至杖六十，增為千四百五十貫，餘杖各遞加二百貫，成化二年，令婦人犯法贖罪。

translations.literal: up to sixty rod blows, increased to one thousand four hundred fifty strings; for remaining rod gradations each increased by two hundred strings. In the second year of Chenghua, ordered that women who violated the law might ransom crimes.
translations.idiomatic: reaching one thousand four hundred fifty strings at sixty blows of the rod, with two hundred strings added for each further rod gradation. In the second year of Chenghua, women who broke the law were permitted to ransom their punishment.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年，定折收銀錢之制。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, fixed the system of collecting silver and coin by conversion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, a system was established for accepting ransom in silver and coin by conversion.

sentences.zh: 例難的決人犯，並婦人有力者，每杖百，應鈔二千二百五十貫，折銀一兩；

translations.literal: Offenders whom precedent made difficult to beat on the spot, and women with means—for every hundred rod blows, the paper money due was two thousand two hundred fifty strings, converted to one tael of silver;
translations.idiomatic: Offenders whom precedent exempted from immediate beating, and women of means: for one hundred blows of the rod, two thousand two hundred fifty strings of notes were due, convertible to one tael of silver;

sentences.zh: 每十以二百貫遞減，至杖六十為銀六錢；

translations.literal: for every ten a decrease of two hundred strings, down to sixty rod blows as six mace of silver;
translations.idiomatic: decreasing by two hundred strings for every ten blows, to six mace of silver at sixty blows;

sentences.zh: 笞五十，應減為鈔八百貫，折銀五錢，每十以百五十貫遞減；

translations.literal: fifty cane blows should be reduced to eight hundred strings of notes, converted to five mace of silver; for every ten a decrease of one hundred fifty strings;
translations.idiomatic: fifty blows of the cane: eight hundred strings, convertible to five mace of silver, decreasing by one hundred fifty strings for every ten blows;

sentences.zh: 至笞二十為銀二錢；

translations.literal: down to twenty cane blows as two mace of silver;
translations.idiomatic: down to two mace of silver at twenty blows;

sentences.zh: 笞十應鈔二百貫，折銀一錢。

translations.literal: Ten cane blows due two hundred strings of notes, converted to one mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Ten blows of the cane required two hundred strings of notes, convertible to one mace of silver.

sentences.zh: 如收銅錢，每銀一兩折七百文。

translations.literal: If collecting copper cash, each tael of silver converted to seven hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: If copper cash was accepted, each tael of silver was reckoned at seven hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 其依律贖鈔，除過失殺人外，亦視此數折收。

translations.literal: Those who ransomed paper money according to the Code, apart from negligent homicide, likewise collected conversion at these numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory ransom in paper notes, except for negligent homicide, was likewise collected at these converted rates.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，定錢鈔兼收之制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, fixed the system of collecting coin and paper money together.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, a system was established for accepting both coin and paper notes.

sentences.zh: 如杖一百，應鈔二千二百五十貫者，收鈔千一百二十五貫，錢三百五十文。

translations.literal: For example, one hundred rod blows, where two thousand two hundred fifty strings of notes were due—collect one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings of notes and three hundred fifty wen of coin.
translations.idiomatic: For example, one hundred blows of the rod, where two thousand two hundred fifty strings were due: collect one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings of notes and three hundred fifty wen in coin.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，巡撫湖廣都御史硃廷聲言：「收贖與贖罪有異，在京與在外不同，鈔貫止聚於都下，錢法不行於南方。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Huguang Zhu Tingsheng said: "Receiving ransom and ransoming crimes differ; in the capital and outside differ; strings of notes gather only in the capital, coin law does not operate in the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Zhu Tingsheng of Huguang reported: "Statutory redemption and pecuniary commutation differ; capital and provinces differ; paper notes circulate chiefly in the capital, while coin does not function in the south.

sentences.zh: 故事，審有力及命婦、軍職正妻，及例難的決者，有贖罪例鈔；

translations.literal: By precedent, when reviewing those with means, titled ladies, principal wives of military officers, and those whom precedent made difficult to beat on the spot—there is ransom-crime precedent paper;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, those found to have means, titled ladies, principal wives of military officers, and those exempt from immediate beating paid under "precedent ransom notes";

sentences.zh: 老幼廢疾及婦人餘罪，有收贖律鈔。

translations.literal: the old, young, disabled, and women's remaining crimes have receiving statutory ransom paper.
translations.idiomatic: the elderly, young, disabled, and women for remaining offenses paid under "Code ransom notes."

sentences.zh: 贖罪例鈔，錢鈔兼收，如笞一十，收鈔百貫，收錢三十五文，其鈔二百貫，折銀一錢。

translations.literal: Ransom-crime precedent paper: coin and notes collected together—for example ten cane blows, collect one hundred strings of notes and thirty-five wen of coin; its two hundred strings of notes convert to one mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For precedent ransom notes, coin and paper were collected together: ten blows of the cane required one hundred strings of notes and thirty-five wen in coin, though the full two hundred strings converted to one mace of silver.

sentences.zh: 杖一百，收鈔千一百二十五貫，收錢三百五十文，其鈔二千二百五十貫，折銀一兩。

translations.literal: One hundred rod blows: collect one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings of notes and three hundred fifty wen of coin; its two thousand two hundred fifty strings of notes convert to one tael of silver.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred blows of the rod: collect one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings and three hundred fifty wen, though the full two thousand two hundred fifty strings converted to one tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 今收贖律鈔，笞一十，止贖六百文，比例鈔折銀不及一釐；

translations.literal: Now receiving statutory ransom paper—for ten cane blows, only six hundred wen ransom; proportionally converting notes to silver does not reach one candareen;
translations.idiomatic: Today, under Code ransom notes, ten blows of the cane require only six hundred wen; converted proportionally to silver, this amounts to less than one candareen;

sentences.zh: 杖一百，贖鈔六貫，折銀不及一分，似為太輕。

translations.literal: one hundred rod blows, ransom six strings of notes, converting to silver not reaching one fen—seems too light.
translations.idiomatic: one hundred blows of the rod requires only six strings of notes, less than one fen in silver—far too lenient.

sentences.zh: 蓋律鈔與例鈔，貫既不同，則折銀亦當有異。

translations.literal: For Code notes and precedent notes, since the strings differ, conversion to silver should also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Since Code notes and precedent notes use different string counts, their silver conversions should likewise differ.

sentences.zh: 請更定為則，凡收贖者，每鈔一貫，折銀一分二釐五毫。

translations.literal: I request that the rule be newly fixed: for all who receive ransom, each string of notes converts to one fen two candareen five cash of silver.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a new rule be set: for all statutory redemptions, each string of notes shall convert to one fen, two candareen, and five cash of silver.

sentences.zh: 如笞一十，贖鈔六百文，則折銀七釐五毫，以罪重輕遞加折收贖。」

translations.literal: For example ten cane blows, ransom six hundred wen of notes, then converts to seven candareen five cash of silver; according to the crime's heaviness or lightness, increase stepwise in collecting converted ransom."
translations.idiomatic: For example, ten blows of the cane at six hundred wen in notes would convert to seven candareen and five cash of silver, with graduated increases according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 帝從其奏，令中外問刑諸司，皆以此例從事。

translations.literal: ] The emperor followed his memorial and ordered all judicial offices inside and outside to proceed by this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial and ordered all judicial offices at home and abroad to follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 是時重修條例，奏定贖例。

translations.literal: At this time the regulations were newly revised and ransom precedents were memorialized and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the regulations were revised and ransom precedents were memorialized and enacted.

sentences.zh: 在京則做工、每笞一十，做工一月，折銀三錢。

translations.literal: In the capital then labor service: for every ten cane blows, one month of labor, converted to three mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, labor service applied: every ten blows of the cane required one month of labor, convertible to three mace of silver.

sentences.zh: 至徒五年，折銀十八兩。

translations.literal: Up to five years of penal servitude, converted to eighteen taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Up to five years of penal servitude, convertible to eighteen taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 運囚糧、每笞一十，米五斗，折銀二錢五分。

translations.literal: Transporting convict grain: for every ten cane blows, five dou of rice, converted to two mace five candareen of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Transporting convict grain: every ten blows of the cane required five dou of rice, convertible to two mace and five candareen of silver.

sentences.zh: 至徒五年，五十石，折銀二十五兩。

translations.literal: Up to five years of penal servitude, fifty shi, converted to twenty-five taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Up to five years of penal servitude, fifty shi of grain, convertible to twenty-five taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 運灰、每笞一十，一千二百斤，折銀一兩二錢六分。

translations.literal: Transporting lime: for every ten cane blows, one thousand two hundred jin, converted to one tael two mace six fen of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Transporting lime: every ten blows of the cane required one thousand two hundred jin, convertible to one tael, two mace, and six fen of silver.

sentences.zh: 至徒五年，六萬斤，折銀六十三兩。

translations.literal: Up to five years of penal servitude, sixty thousand jin, converted to sixty-three taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Up to five years of penal servitude, sixty thousand jin of lime, convertible to sixty-three taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 運磚、每笞一十，七十個，折銀九錢一分。

translations.literal: Transporting bricks: for every ten cane blows, seventy pieces, converted to nine mace one fen of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Transporting bricks: every ten blows of the cane required seventy bricks, convertible to nine mace and one fen of silver.

sentences.zh: 至徒五年，三千個，折銀三十九兩。

translations.literal: Up to five years of penal servitude, three thousand pieces, converted to thirty-nine taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Up to five years of penal servitude, three thousand bricks, convertible to thirty-nine taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 運水和炭五等。

translations.literal: Transporting water and charcoal—five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Transporting water and charcoal were ranked in five grades.

sentences.zh: 每笞一十，二百斤，折銀四錢。

translations.literal: For every ten cane blows, two hundred jin, converted to four mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten blows of the cane required two hundred jin, convertible to four mace of silver.

sentences.zh: 至徒五年，八千五百斤，折銀十七兩。

translations.literal: Up to five years of penal servitude, eight thousand five hundred jin, converted to seventeen taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Up to five years of penal servitude, eight thousand five hundred jin, convertible to seventeen taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 運灰最重，運炭最輕。

translations.literal: Transporting lime was heaviest; transporting charcoal was lightest.
translations.idiomatic: Hauling lime carried the heaviest burden; hauling charcoal the lightest.

sentences.zh: 在外則有力、稍有力二等。

translations.literal: Outside the capital there were two grades: you li and shao you li.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces there were only two classes: those with means and those somewhat with means.

sentences.zh: 初有頗有力、次有力等，因御史言而革。

translations.literal: At first there were po you li, ci you li, and the like; abolished on a censor's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At first there had also been grades such as "quite with means" and "next with means," but these were abolished after a censor's memorial.

sentences.zh: 其有力，視在京運囚糧，每米五斗，納谷一石。

translations.literal: For you li, it followed capital transport of convict grain: for every five dou of rice, deliver one shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: For those with means, the rate followed capital convict-grain transport: every five dou of rice due was commuted by delivering one shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 初折銀上庫，後折穀上倉。

translations.literal: At first silver was converted and paid to the state treasury; later grain was converted and paid to the granary.
translations.idiomatic: At first commutation was paid in silver to the state treasury; later it was paid in grain to the public granary.

sentences.zh: 稍有力，視在京做工年月為折贖。

translations.literal: Shao you li followed capital labor by months and years for converted ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Those somewhat with means commuted according to the months and years of labor service fixed for the capital.

sentences.zh: 婦人審有力，與命婦、軍職正妻，及例難的決之人，贖罪應錢鈔兼收者，笞、杖每一十，折收銀一錢。

translations.literal: Women found with means, with titled ladies and principal wives of military officers, and those whom precedent made difficult to beat on the spot—where ransom-crime required collecting coin and notes together—for every ten cane or rod blows, collect one mace of silver by conversion.
translations.idiomatic: Women found to have means, titled ladies, principal wives of military officers, and those exempt from immediate beating who owed combined coin-and-note ransom: for every ten blows of cane or rod, one mace of silver was collected by conversion.

sentences.zh: 其老幼廢疾婦人及天文生餘罪收贖者，每笞一十應鈔六百文，折收銀七釐五毫。

translations.literal: For the old, young, disabled, women, and astronomical clerks whose remaining crimes received statutory ransom—for every ten cane blows six hundred wen of notes were due, collected as seven candareen five cash of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For the elderly, young, disabled, women, and astronomical clerks redeeming remaining offenses under the Code: every ten blows of the cane required six hundred wen in notes, collected as seven candareen and five cash of silver.

sentences.zh: 於是輕重適均，天下便之。

translations.literal: Thus heavy and light were properly balanced, and all under Heaven found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Thus penalties were properly balanced in severity, and the realm found the system workable.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆十三年，復申明焉，遂為定制。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year of Wanli it was again proclaimed and clarified, and thereafter became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Wanli the rules were proclaimed again, and thereafter they became permanent statute.

sentences.zh: 凡律贖，若天文生習業已成、能專其事、犯徒及流者，決杖一百，餘罪收贖。

translations.literal: For all statutory ransom: if an astronomical clerk's training is complete and he can devote himself to the art, and he commits penal servitude or exile—impose one hundred rod blows; redeem the remaining crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Under statutory ransom, if an astronomical clerk had completed his training and could practice his art exclusively, yet committed penal servitude or exile, he received one hundred blows of the rod and redeemed the remaining offenses.

sentences.zh: 婦人犯徒流者，決杖一百，餘罪收贖。

translations.literal: Women who commit penal servitude or exile: impose one hundred rod blows; redeem the remaining crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Women guilty of penal servitude or exile received one hundred blows of the rod and redeemed the remaining offenses.

sentences.zh: 如杖六十，徒一年，全贖鈔應十二貫，除決杖準訖六貫，餘鈔六貫，折銀七分五釐，餘仿此。

translations.literal: For example sixty rod blows and one year of penal servitude: full ransom in notes should be twelve strings; deducting the imposed rod blows reckoned at six strings completed, remaining notes six strings, converted to seven candareen five cash of silver—the rest follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: For example, sixty blows of the rod plus one year of penal servitude: full ransom required twelve strings of notes; deducting six strings for the imposed blows, six strings remained, convertible to seven candareen and five cash of silver—and so on for other cases.

sentences.zh: 其決杖一百，審有力又納例鈔二千二百五十貫，應收錢三百五十文，鈔一千一百二十五貫。

translations.literal: When one hundred rod blows were imposed, those found with means who also paid precedent notes of two thousand two hundred fifty strings should pay three hundred fifty wen of coin and one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: When one hundred blows of the rod were imposed, those of means who also paid precedent ransom owed three hundred fifty wen in coin and one thousand one hundred twenty-five strings of notes out of the full two thousand two hundred fifty strings.

sentences.zh: 凡年七十以上十五以下及廢疾犯流以下，收贖；

translations.literal: All aged seventy and above or fifteen and below, and the disabled who commit exile or below, receive ransom;
translations.idiomatic: All persons seventy or older, fifteen or younger, and the disabled who committed exile or lesser offenses were permitted statutory redemption;

sentences.zh: 八十以上十歲以下及篤疾、盜及傷人者，亦收贖。

translations.literal: eighty and above or ten and below, and those gravely ill, and theft and wounding, also receive ransom.
translations.idiomatic: as did those eighty or older or ten or younger, the gravely ill, and offenders guilty of theft or wounding.

sentences.zh: 凡犯罪時未老疾，事發時老疾者，依老疾論，犯罪時幼小，事發時長大者，依幼小論，並得收贖。

translations.literal: All who at the time of the crime were not old or ill but at the time the matter arose were old or ill are judged as old or ill; who at the crime were young but at the matter arose had grown are judged as young—all may receive ransom.
translations.idiomatic: If one was not old or ill at the time of the offense but was so when the case arose, he was judged as old or ill; if young at the offense but grown when the case arose, he was judged as young—in either case redemption was allowed.

sentences.zh: 如六十九以下犯罪，年七十事發，或無疾時犯罪，廢疾後事發，得依老疾收贖。

translations.literal: For example, crime below sixty-nine, matter arises at seventy; or crime when without disability, matter arises after disability—may receive ransom according to old age or disability.
translations.idiomatic: For example, one who committed a crime before sixty-nine but whose case arose at seventy, or who was healthy at the crime but disabled when the case arose, could redeem under the rules for age or disability.

sentences.zh: 他或七十九以下犯死罪，八十事發，或廢疾時犯罪，篤疾時事發，得入上請。

translations.literal: Otherwise, capital crime below seventy-nine, matter arises at eighty; or crime when disabled, matter arises when gravely ill—may enter petition above.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, one who committed a capital crime before seventy-nine but whose case arose at eighty, or who was merely disabled at the crime but gravely ill when the case arose, might petition the throne for mercy.

sentences.zh: 八十九犯死罪，九十事發，得勿論，不在收贖之例。

translations.literal: Capital crime at eighty-nine, matter arises at ninety—may be not punished; not within the precedent of receiving ransom.
translations.idiomatic: One who committed a capital crime at eighty-nine but whose case arose at ninety was exempt from punishment altogether and fell outside the rules for statutory redemption.

sentences.zh: 若在徒年限內老疾，亦如之。

translations.literal: If within the term of penal servitude one becomes old or ill, it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied if one became old or ill while still serving a term of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 如犯杖六十，徒一年，一月之後老疾，合計全贖鈔十二貫。

translations.literal: For example, offense of sixty rod blows and one year penal servitude; one month later old or ill—the full ransom in notes totals twelve strings.
translations.idiomatic: For example, for sixty blows of the rod and one year of penal servitude, if one became old or ill after one month of service, the full ransom in notes totaled twelve strings.

sentences.zh: 除已杖六十，準三貫六百文，剩徒一年，應八貫四百文計算。

translations.literal: Deducting the already imposed sixty rod blows reckoned at three strings six hundred wen, remaining one year penal servitude should be reckoned at eight strings four hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: Deducting three strings six hundred wen for the sixty blows already imposed, the remaining year of penal servitude was reckoned at eight strings four hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 每徒一月，贖鈔七百文，已役一月，準贖七百文外，未贖十一月，應收贖七貫七百文。

translations.literal: Each month of penal servitude, ransom seven hundred wen of notes; one month already served reckoned at seven hundred wen ransom besides, eleven months not yet ransomed should receive ransom of seven strings seven hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: Each month of servitude required seven hundred wen in notes; with one month already served counted as seven hundred wen, the eleven months remaining required seven strings seven hundred wen in ransom.

sentences.zh: 餘仿此。

translations.literal: The rest follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Other cases followed the same method of calculation.

sentences.zh: 老幼廢疾收贖，惟雜犯五年仍科之。

translations.literal: Old, young, and disabled receive ransom, but miscellaneous offenses of five years are still sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: The elderly, young, and disabled might redeem their penalties, but miscellaneous offenses carrying five years of servitude were still fully imposed.

sentences.zh: 蓋在明初，即真犯死罪，不可以徒論也

translations.literal: For at the beginning of Ming, even true capital offenders could not be judged as penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: This reflected early Ming severity, when even principal capital crimes were not commuted to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 其誣告例，告二事以上，輕實重虛，或告一事，誣輕為重者，已論決全抵剩罪，未論決笞杖收贖，徒流杖一百，餘罪亦聽收贖。

translations.literal: The false-accusation precedent: accusing on two matters or more with light truth and heavy falsehood, or accusing on one matter with light falsely made heavy—what is already judged and decided fully offsets remaining crime; what is not yet judged and decided, cane and rod receive ransom; penal servitude and exile receive one hundred rod blows, remaining crimes also permitted ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Under the false-accusation precedent, if one accused another of two or more matters with the lighter proven and the heavier false, or exaggerated a single charge, sentences already imposed fully offset the remainder; unadjudicated cane and rod offenses could be redeemed; for penal servitude or exile the accuser received one hundred blows of the rod and might redeem any remaining penalty.

sentences.zh: 如告人笞三十，內止一十實已決，全抵，剩二十之罪未決，收贖一貫二百文。

translations.literal: For example, accusing someone of thirty cane blows, of which only ten were true and already decided—fully offset; remaining twenty blows' crime undecided, receive ransom one string two hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: For example, if one falsely accused another of thirty blows of the cane, of which only ten were true and already imposed, those ten fully offset the penalty; for the remaining twenty blows not yet adjudicated, ransom of one string two hundred wen was due.

sentences.zh: 如告人杖六十，內止二十實已決，全抵，剩四十之罪未決，收贖二貫四百文。

translations.literal: For example, accusing someone of sixty rod blows, of which only twenty were true and already decided—fully offset; remaining forty blows' crime undecided, receive ransom two strings four hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: If one accused another of sixty blows of the rod, of which only twenty were true and already imposed, those twenty fully offset the penalty; for the remaining forty blows, ransom of two strings four hundred wen was due.

sentences.zh: 如告人杖六十，徒一年，內止杖五十實已決，全抵，剩杖一十、徒一年之罪未決，徒一年，折杖六十，並杖共七十，收贖四貫二百文。

translations.literal: For example, accusing someone of sixty rod blows and one year penal servitude, of which only fifty rod blows were true and already decided—fully offset; remaining ten rod blows and one year penal servitude undecided; one year penal servitude converts to sixty rod blows, total rod blows seventy, receive ransom four strings two hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: If one accused another of sixty blows of the rod plus one year of penal servitude, but only fifty blows were true and already imposed, those fifty fully offset the penalty; for the remaining ten blows and one year of servitude, the year converted to sixty blows, seventy blows in all, requiring ransom of four strings two hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 如告人杖一百，流二千里，內止杖六十、徒一年實已決，以總徒四年論，全抵，剩杖四十、徒三年之罪未決，以連徒折杖流加一等論，共計杖二百二十，除告實杖六十、徒一年，折杖六十，剩杖一百，贖鈔六貫。

translations.literal: For example, accusing someone of one hundred rod blows and exile two thousand li, of which only sixty rod blows and one year penal servitude were true and already decided—reckoned as total four years penal servitude, fully offset; remaining forty rod blows and three years penal servitude undecided—reckoned by linked penal servitude converting rod blows and exile increased one grade, total rod blows two hundred twenty; deducting the true accusation of sixty rod blows and one year penal servitude converting to sixty rod blows, remaining one hundred rod blows, ransom six strings of notes.
