translations.idiomatic: If one accused another of one hundred blows of the rod and exile two thousand li, but only sixty blows and one year of servitude were true and already imposed, reckoned as four years of servitude in all, those fully offset the penalty; for the remaining forty blows and three years of servitude, reckoned by converting linked servitude to blows and raising exile one grade, the total came to two hundred twenty blows; deducting the sixty blows and one year actually proved (the year converting to sixty blows), one hundred blows remained, requiring ransom of six strings of notes.

sentences.zh: 若計剩罪，過杖一百以上，須決杖一百訖，餘罪方聽收贖。

translations.literal: If reckoning remaining crime exceeds one hundred rod blows, one must impose one hundred rod blows completed before remaining crime is permitted ransom.
translations.idiomatic: If the remaining penalty exceeded one hundred blows of the rod, the accuser had to receive the full one hundred blows before redeeming any remainder.

sentences.zh: 又過失傷人，淮鬥毆傷人罪，依律收贖。

translations.literal: Also, negligent wounding follows the crime of brawling and wounding, receiving ransom according to the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Negligent wounding, too, was treated like brawling and wounding and redeemed according to the Code.

sentences.zh: 至死者，準雜犯斬絞收贖，鈔四十二貫。

translations.literal: Reaching death, follow miscellaneous offenses' decapitation and strangulation ransom—forty-two strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: If death resulted, ransom followed the rates for miscellaneous capital offenses—forty-two strings of notes.

sentences.zh: 內鈔八分，應三十三貫六百文，銅錢二分，應八千四百文，給付其家。

translations.literal: Of this, eight-tenths in notes should be thirty-three strings six hundred wen, two-tenths in copper cash should be eight thousand four hundred wen, paid to the family.
translations.idiomatic: Of this sum, eight-tenths in notes came to thirty-three strings six hundred wen, and two-tenths in copper cash to eight thousand four hundred wen, paid to the victim's family.

sentences.zh: 已徒五年，再犯徒收贖。

translations.literal: Having completed five years penal servitude, again committing penal servitude receives ransom.
translations.idiomatic: One who had already served five years of penal servitude and committed penal servitude again could redeem the penalty.

sentences.zh: 鈔三十六貫。

translations.literal: Thirty-six strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: The ransom was thirty-six strings of notes.

sentences.zh: 若犯徒流，存留養親者，止杖一百，餘罪收贖。

translations.literal: If committing penal servitude or exile, retained to support parents—only one hundred rod blows; redeem remaining crimes.
translations.idiomatic: If one guilty of penal servitude or exile was retained to support parents, he received only one hundred blows of the rod and redeemed the remaining offenses.

sentences.zh: 其法實杖一百，不準折贖，然後計徒流年限，一視老幼例贖之。

translations.literal: The law actually imposes one hundred rod blows, not permitting converted ransom; then reckons penal servitude and exile years, uniformly following the old-and-young precedent for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: The law required the full one hundred blows without commutation, then calculated the years of servitude or exile and applied the same redemption rates as for the elderly and young.

sentences.zh: 此律自英宗時詔有司行之，後為制。

translations.literal: This statute from the time of Emperor Yingzong was ordered implemented by the responsible offices, and later became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This rule was ordered into practice under Emperor Yingzong and later became permanent statute.

sentences.zh: 天文生、婦女犯徒流，決杖一百，餘罪收贖者，雖罪止杖六十，徒一年，亦決杖一百，律所謂應加杖者是也。

translations.literal: Astronomical clerks and women who commit penal servitude or exile, impose one hundred rod blows and redeem remaining crimes—even if the crime stops at sixty rod blows and one year penal servitude, still impose one hundred rod blows; this is what the Code calls the rod blows that should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical clerks and women guilty of penal servitude or exile received one hundred blows of the rod and redeemed the rest—even when the offense itself called for only sixty blows and one year of servitude, they still received one hundred blows, the Code's "supplementary beating."

sentences.zh: 皆先依本律議，其所犯徒流之罪，以《誥》減之。

translations.literal: All first deliberate according to the original Code; the penal servitude and exile crimes committed are reduced by the Grand Pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment proceeded first under the Code itself, with penal servitude and exile reduced according to the Grand Pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 至臨決時，某系天文生，某系婦人，依律決杖一百，餘收贖。

translations.literal: At the time of imminent beating, if someone is an astronomical clerk or a woman, according to the Code impose one hundred rod blows; redeem the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution, if the offender was an astronomical clerk or a woman, the court imposed one hundred blows of the rod under the Code and allowed redemption of the remainder.

sentences.zh: 所決之杖並須一百者，包五徒之數也。

translations.literal: The imposed rod blows all requiring one hundred encompass the number of the five grades of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The requirement of a full one hundred blows encompassed all five grades of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 然與誣告收贖剩杖不同。

translations.literal: Yet it differs from false accusation's receiving ransom for remaining rod blows.
translations.idiomatic: This differed from the false-accusation rule for redeeming remaining blows.

sentences.zh: 蓋收贖餘徒者決杖，而贖徒收贖剩杖者，折流歸徒，折徒歸杖，而照數收贖之，其法各別也。

translations.literal: For receiving ransom of remaining penal servitude one imposes rod blows; but for ransoming penal servitude and receiving ransom for remaining rod blows, convert exile to penal servitude, penal servitude to rod blows, and receive ransom according to the number—the methods each differ.
translations.idiomatic: In one case rod blows were imposed before redeeming remaining servitude; in the other, exile was converted to servitude and servitude to blows, with ransom calculated accordingly—the two procedures were distinct.

sentences.zh: 其婦人犯徒流，成化八年定例，除奸盜不孝與樂婦外，若審有力並決杖，亦得以納鈔贖罪。

translations.literal: For women who commit penal servitude or exile, precedent fixed in the eighth year of Chenghua: apart from adultery, theft, unfilial conduct, and licensed courtesans, if found with means and also imposed rod blows, they may also ransom crimes by paying notes.
translations.idiomatic: For women guilty of penal servitude or exile, a precedent of the eighth year of Chenghua held that except in cases of adultery, theft, unfilial conduct, or licensed courtesans, women of means who also received the rod might commute their penalties by paying notes.

sentences.zh: 例每杖十，折銀一錢為率，至杖一百，折銀一兩止。

translations.literal: Precedent: every ten rod blows, one mace of silver as the rate, up to one hundred rod blows stopping at one tael of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The rate was one mace of silver for every ten blows of the rod, up to a maximum of one tael for one hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 凡律所謂收贖者，贖餘罪也。

translations.literal: All that the Code calls receiving ransom is redeeming remaining crimes.
translations.idiomatic: What the Code called "statutory redemption" meant redeeming the remaining offenses.

sentences.zh: 其例得贖罪者，贖決杖一百也。

translations.literal: Those whom precedent permits to ransom crimes ransom the imposed one hundred rod blows.
translations.idiomatic: What precedent allowed as "pecuniary commutation" meant redeeming the imposed one hundred blows of the rod.

sentences.zh: 徒、杖兩項分科之，除婦人，餘囚徒流皆杖決不贖。

translations.literal: Penal servitude and rod blows are sentenced as two separate items; apart from women, all other convicts for penal servitude and exile are rod-imposed and not ransomed.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude and the rod were sentenced separately; except for women, all other offenders guilty of servitude or exile were beaten and not permitted to commute the blows.

sentences.zh: 惟弘治十三年，許樂戶徒杖笞罪，亦不的決，此律鈔之大凡也。

translations.literal: Only in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi were licensed households permitted penal servitude, rod, and cane crimes also not beaten on the spot—this is the general outline of Code notes.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi were licensed entertainers' offenses of servitude, rod, and cane likewise exempted from immediate beating—such was the general scope of Code ransom.

sentences.zh: 例鈔自嘉靖二十九年定例。

translations.literal: Precedent notes were fixed as precedent from the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent ransom rates were established in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 凡軍民諸色人役及舍餘審有力者，與文武官吏、監生、生員、冠帶官、知印、承差、陰陽生、醫生、老人、舍人，不分笞、杖、徒、流、雜犯死罪，俱令運灰、運炭、運磚、納米、納料等項贖罪。

translations.literal: All military and civilian persons of various services and surplus-household members found with means, together with civil and military officials, students of the Imperial Academy, licentiates, officials with ceremonial sashes, seal keepers, dispatch clerks, yin-yang clerks, physicians, elders, and household retainers—regardless of cane, rod, penal servitude, exile, or miscellaneous capital crimes—all were ordered to transport lime, transport charcoal, transport bricks, deliver rice, deliver materials, and such items to ransom crimes.
translations.idiomatic: All soldiers and civilians in various services, surplus households found to have means, and civil and military officials, Academy students, licentiates, sash-wearing officers, seal keepers, dispatch clerks, yin-yang specialists, physicians, village elders, and household retainers—whatever the offense, from cane and rod through servitude, exile, and miscellaneous capital crimes—were required to commute penalties by hauling lime or charcoal or bricks, delivering rice or materials, and the like.

sentences.zh: 此上系不虧行止者。

translations.literal: The above concern those whose conduct is not impaired.
translations.idiomatic: The above applied to those whose personal conduct was not compromised.

sentences.zh: 若官吏人等，例應革去職役，此係行止有虧者。

translations.literal: If officials and the like, by precedent should be dismissed from office and service—this concerns those whose conduct is impaired.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who by precedent should be stripped of office and rank fell into the category of compromised conduct.

sentences.zh: 與軍民人等審無力者，笞、杖罪的決，徒、流、雜犯死罪各做工、擺站、哨暿愰、發充儀從，情重者煎鹽炒鐵。

translations.literal: Together with military and civilian persons found without means: cane and rod crimes are beaten on the spot; penal servitude, exile, and miscellaneous capital crimes each labor, relay-station duty, frontier sentry posts, or assignment as ceremonial attendants; where the circumstances are grave, boiling salt and smelting iron.
translations.idiomatic: Together with soldiers and civilians found without means: cane and rod offenses were beaten on the spot; penal servitude, exile, and miscellaneous capital crimes were punished by labor, relay-station service, frontier sentry duty, or assignment as ceremonial attendants, with the gravest cases sent to boil salt or smelt iron.

sentences.zh: 死罪五年，流罪四年，徒按年限。

translations.literal: Capital crimes five years, exile crimes four years, penal servitude according to the term of years.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous capital offenses carried five years of labor, exile four years, and penal servitude the statutory term.

sentences.zh: 其在京軍丁人等，無差佔者與例難的決之人，笞杖亦令做工。

translations.literal: Those in the capital such as military conscripts without assignment or requisition, and those whom precedent made difficult to beat on the spot—for cane and rod also ordered to labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, military conscripts without active assignment and those exempt from immediate beating were likewise assigned labor for cane and rod offenses.

sentences.zh: 時新例，犯奸盜受贓，為行止有虧之人，概不許贖罪。

translations.literal: At the time a new precedent: adultery, theft, and accepting bribes—persons whose conduct is impaired—altogether not permitted to ransom crimes.
translations.idiomatic: A recent precedent barred commutation altogether for those guilty of adultery, theft, or bribery—offenses that compromised one's conduct.

sentences.zh: 唯軍官革職者，俱運炭納米等項發落，不用五刑條例的決實配之文，所以寬武夫，重責文吏也。

translations.literal: Only dismissed military officers—all dispatched by transporting charcoal, delivering rice, and such items, not using the five-punishments regulations' text on beating on the spot and actual assignment; thereby leniency toward warriors and heavier responsibility toward civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Only dismissed military officers were punished by hauling charcoal, delivering rice, and the like, without the provisions for immediate beating and actual assignment—leniency toward fighting men and stricter demands on civil officials.

sentences.zh: 於是在京惟行做工、運囚糧等五項，在外惟行有力、稍有力二項，法令益徑省矣。

translations.literal: Thus in the capital only five items were implemented: labor, transporting convict grain, and the like; outside only two items: you li and shao you li—the laws and orders grew ever more direct and simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the capital only five forms of commutation remained—labor, convict-grain transport, and the like—while in the provinces only the two classes of means applied, and the law grew ever more streamlined.

sentences.zh: 要而論之，律鈔輕，例鈔重。

translations.literal: In sum, Code notes are light, precedent notes heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In short, Code ransom was light and precedent ransom heavy.

sentences.zh: 然律鈔本非輕也。

translations.literal: Yet Code notes in origin were not light.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Code ransom had not originally been lenient at all.

sentences.zh: 祖制每鈔一文，當銀一釐，所謂笞一十折鈔六百文定銀七釐五毫者，即當時之銀六錢也。

translations.literal: Ancestral regulation: each wen of notes equals one candareen of silver; what is called ten cane blows converting to six hundred wen of notes fixed at seven candareen five cash of silver—that is six mace of silver at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding regulation each wen of paper money equaled one candareen of silver; the rate of six hundred wen for ten blows of the cane, fixed at seven candareen and five cash of silver, represented six mace of silver at the time.

sentences.zh: 所謂杖一百折鈔六貫銀七分五釐者，即當時之銀六兩也。

translations.literal: What is called one hundred rod blows converting to six strings of notes and seven candareen five cash of silver—that is six taels of silver at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, one hundred blows of the rod at six strings of notes, fixed at seven candareen and five cash of silver, represented six taels of silver at the time.

sentences.zh: 以銀六錢，比例鈔折銀不及一釐，以銀一兩，比例鈔折銀不及一分，而欲以此懲犯罪者之心，宜其勢有所不行矣。

translations.literal: With six mace of silver, proportionally converting notes to silver does not reach one candareen; with one tael of silver, proportionally converting notes to silver does not reach one fen—yet wishing by this to chasten the hearts of criminals, it is fitting that the force could not fully operate.
translations.idiomatic: Six mace of silver in nominal value converted to less than one candareen; one tael converted to less than one fen—yet the state expected such sums to deter crime; small wonder the system could not function as intended.

sentences.zh: 特以祖宗律文不可改也，於是不得已定為七釐五毫、七分五釐之制。

translations.literal: Only because the ancestral Code text could not be altered, therefore unavoidably fixed the system of seven candareen five cash and seven candareen five fen.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ancestral Code could not be altered, the state was forced to fix commutation at seven candareen and five cash for cane offenses and seven candareen and five fen for rod offenses.

sentences.zh: 而其實所定之數，猶不足以當所贖者之罪，然後例之變通生焉。

translations.literal: Yet in fact the numbers fixed still were insufficient to match the crimes of those who ransomed—thence the flexibilities of precedent arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even these fixed sums scarcely matched the gravity of the offenses redeemed—and so the flexible precedents arose.

sentences.zh: 考洪武朝，官吏軍民犯罪聽贖者，大抵罰役之令居多，如發鳳陽屯種、滁州種苜蓿、代農民力役、運米輸邊贖罪之類，俱不用鈔納也。

translations.literal: Examining the Hongwu reign, officials, soldiers, and civilians whose crimes were permitted ransom were mostly orders of penal labor—for example, sent to Fengyang to garrison-farm, to Chuzhou to plant alfalfa, to substitute for peasants' corvée labor, to transport rice to the frontier to ransom crimes—altogether not using payment in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, officials, soldiers, and civilians permitted to commute penalties were chiefly assigned penal labor—garrison farming at Fengyang, planting alfalfa at Chuzhou, substituting for peasants' corvée, transporting rice to the frontier—rather than paying in paper notes.

sentences.zh: 律之所載，笞若干，鈔若干文，杖若干，鈔若干貫者，垂一代之法也。

translations.literal: What the Code records—so many cane blows, so many wen of notes; so many rod blows, so many strings of notes—was the law handed down for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: The Code's tables of blows and note amounts were meant to endure as the law of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然按三十年詔令，罪囚運米贖罪，死罪百石，徒流遞減，其力不及者，死罪自備米三十石，徒流十五石，俱運納甘州、威虜，就彼充軍。

translations.literal: Yet according to the thirtieth-year edict, convicts transported rice to ransom crimes: capital crimes one hundred shi, penal servitude and exile decreasing stepwise; those whose strength did not reach it—capital crimes self-provided thirty shi, penal servitude and exile fifteen shi—all transported and delivered to Ganzhou and Weilu, and there enrolled as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a thirtieth-year edict allowed convicts to commute penalties by transporting rice—one hundred shi for capital crimes, with decreasing amounts for servitude and exile; those unable to manage the full load provided thirty shi for capital offenses or fifteen for servitude and exile, delivered to Ganzhou and Weilu, where they were enrolled as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 計其米價、腳價之費，與鈔數差不相遠，其定為贖鈔之等第，固不輕於後來之例矣。

translations.literal: Reckoning the cost of rice price and transport fees, it differed little from the number of notes; the grades fixed for ransom notes were certainly not lighter than later precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Counting the cost of grain and transport, the burden was scarcely less than the note amounts required—and the Code's ransom scales were hardly lighter than later precedents.

sentences.zh: 然罪無一定，而鈔法之久，日變日輕，此定律時所不及料也。

translations.literal: Yet crimes have no fixed standard, while the paper-note system over time daily changed and daily grew light—this the framers of the Code could not foresee.
translations.idiomatic: Yet offenses varied in gravity while paper money depreciated year by year—something the Code's framers could not have foreseen.

sentences.zh: 即以永樂十一年令「斬罪情輕者，贖鈔八千貫，絞及榜例死罪六千貫。」

translations.literal: Take even the eleventh-year Yongle order: "For decapitation where the circumstances are light, ransom eight thousand strings of notes; for strangulation and posted-precedent capital crimes, six thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Consider even the eleventh-year Yongle order: "For decapitation where circumstances were light, ransom eight thousand strings of notes; for strangulation and posted-precedent capital crimes, six thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 之詔言之，八千貫者，律之八千兩也；

translations.literal: Speaking of that edict—eight thousand strings were the Code's eight thousand taels;
translations.idiomatic: By that edict's logic, eight thousand strings equaled eight thousand taels under the Code;

sentences.zh: 六千貫者，律之六千兩也；

translations.literal: six thousand strings were the Code's six thousand taels;
translations.idiomatic: six thousand strings equaled six thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 下至杖罪千貫，笞罪五百貫，亦一千兩、五百兩也。

translations.literal: down to rod crimes one thousand strings, cane crimes five hundred strings—also one thousand taels and five hundred taels.
translations.idiomatic: down to one thousand strings for rod offenses and five hundred for cane offenses—one thousand and five hundred taels respectively.

sentences.zh: 雖革除之際，用法特苛，豈有死罪納至八千兩，笞杖罪納至一千兩、五百兩而尚可行者？

translations.literal: Although at the time of reform the use of law was especially harsh, could there be capital crimes paying up to eight thousand taels, cane and rod crimes paying up to one thousand and five hundred taels, and still be workable?
translations.idiomatic: Even allowing that Yongle applied the law with special severity, who could pay eight thousand taels for a capital offense, or one thousand or five hundred for cane and rod crimes, and still call the system workable?

sentences.zh: 則知鈔法之弊，在永樂初年，已不啻輕十倍於洪武時矣。

translations.literal: Then one knows the defect of the note system: by the beginning of Yongle it was already no less than ten times lighter than Hongwu times.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that paper money had already depreciated at least tenfold from Hongwu levels by the early Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，申交易用銀之禁，冀通鈔法。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign, the prohibition on trading and using silver was proclaimed anew, hoping to revive the note system.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande the ban on private silver transactions was renewed in hope of reviving paper currency.

sentences.zh: 至弘治而鈔竟不可用，遂開準鈔折銀之例。

translations.literal: By Hongzhi notes were finally unusable, and then the precedent of converting according to notes into silver was opened.
translations.idiomatic: By Hongzhi paper notes had become altogether unusable, and the precedent of converting statutory note amounts into silver was established.

sentences.zh: 及嘉靖新定條例，俱以有力、稍有力二科贖罪：有力米五斗，準律之納鈔六百文也；

translations.literal: When Jiajing newly fixed regulations, all used you li and shao you li two grades to ransom crimes: you li five dou of rice, equivalent to the Code's payment of six hundred wen of notes;
translations.idiomatic: When Jiajing enacted new regulations, commutation fell under the two classes of means: those with means paid five dou of rice, equivalent to the Code's six hundred wen in notes;

sentences.zh: 稍有力工價三錢，準律之做工一月也。

translations.literal: shao you li labor price three mace, equivalent to the Code's one month of labor.
translations.idiomatic: those somewhat with means paid three mace in labor wages, equivalent to one month's labor under the Code.

sentences.zh: 是則後之例鈔，才足比於初之律鈔耳。

translations.literal: Thus later precedent notes only just suffice to compare with early Code notes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus later precedent ransom only roughly matched the weight of early Code ransom.

sentences.zh: 而況老幼廢疾，諸在律贖者之銀七釐五毫，準鈔六百文，銀七分五釐，準鈔六貫。

translations.literal: Moreover the old, young, and disabled—all under statutory ransom—silver seven candareen five cash equivalent to six hundred wen of notes; silver seven candareen five fen equivalent to six strings of notes.
translations.idiomatic: As for the elderly, young, and disabled under statutory redemption—seven candareen and five cash of silver for six hundred wen in notes, seven candareen and five fen for six strings—the gap was far wider.

sentences.zh: 凡所謂律贖者，以比於初之律鈔，其輕重相去尤甚懸絕乎？

translations.literal: All that is called statutory ransom—compared with early Code notes, are heavy and light not especially far apart?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the original Code ransom, was statutory redemption not vastly lighter still?

sentences.zh: 唯運炭、運石諸罪例稍重，蓋此諸罪，初皆令親自赴役，事完甯家，原無納贖之例。

translations.literal: Only transporting charcoal, transporting stone, and such crimes' precedents were somewhat heavy—for these crimes at first all ordered personal attendance at labor; when the task was done one returned home in peace; originally there was no precedent of paying ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Only the precedents for hauling charcoal and stone were somewhat heavier—for these offenses originally required personal labor, after which one returned home, with no commutation by payment.

sentences.zh: 其後法令益寬，聽其折納，而估算事力，亦略相當，實不為病也。

translations.literal: Later laws and orders grew ever more lenient, permitting converted payment; reckoning labor power also was roughly equivalent—truly no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Later the law grew more lenient and allowed commutation in kind; reckoned against actual labor, the rates were roughly equivalent and posed no real problem.

sentences.zh: 大抵贖例有二：一罰役，一納鈔，而例復三變。

translations.literal: Generally ransom precedents had two kinds: penal labor and paying notes—and precedents again changed three times.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, commutation took two forms—penal labor and payment in notes—and the precedents shifted three times.

sentences.zh: 罰役者，後多折工值納鈔，鈔法既壞，變為納銀、納米。

translations.literal: Penal labor—later mostly converted labor value to paying notes; once the note system was ruined, changed to paying silver and paying rice.
translations.idiomatic: Penal labor was later commuted to note payments at labor rates; when paper money collapsed, commutation shifted to silver and grain.

sentences.zh: 然運灰、運炭、運石、運磚、運碎磚之名尚存也。

translations.literal: Yet the names transporting lime, transporting charcoal, transporting stone, transporting bricks, transporting broken bricks still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the old names survived—hauling lime, charcoal, stone, bricks, and broken brick.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆中年，中外通行有力、稍有力二科，在京諸例，並不見施行，而法益歸一矣。

translations.literal: By the middle years of Wanli, inside and outside universally applied you li and shao you li two grades; capital precedents were altogether no longer seen implemented—and the law grew ever more unified.
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-Wanli reign the two classes of means applied everywhere; the capital's numerous precedents fell into disuse, and the law grew unified at last.

sentences.zh: 所謂通變而無失於古之意者此也。

translations.literal: What is called adapting while not losing the intent of antiquity—is this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the adaptation that preserved the spirit of the ancestral law.

sentences.zh: 初，令罪人得以力役贖罪：死罪拘役終身，徒流按年限，笞杖計日月。

translations.literal: At first it was ordered that criminals might redeem crimes through corvée labor: capital crimes were detained for life, exile and penal servitude by year-limits, cane and rod by day and month.
translations.idiomatic: At first, criminals could commute sentences through labor: capital offenders were held for life, those exiled or sentenced to penal servitude served term by term, and cane or rod punishments by day and month.

sentences.zh: 或修造，或屯種，或煎鹽炒鐵，滿日疏放。

translations.literal: Some did construction, some colony planting, some boiling salt and smelting iron; when the days were full they were released on parole.
translations.idiomatic: They might build, farm colony lands, boil salt, or smelt iron—and when their term was complete, were released.

sentences.zh: 疏放者，引赴禦橋，叩頭畢，送應天府，給引寧家。

translations.literal: Those released on parole were led to the Imperial Bridge; after kowtowing they were sent to Yingtian Prefecture and given a travel warrant to return home in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Paroled prisoners were led to the Imperial Bridge to kowtow, then escorted to Yingtian Prefecture for a travel permit to return home.

sentences.zh: 合充軍者，發付陝西司，按籍編發。

translations.literal: Those fitting military exile were dispatched to the Shaanxi Bureau and assigned according to household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Those due for military exile were sent to the Shaanxi Bureau for registry-based assignment.

sentences.zh: 後皆折納工價，惟赴橋如舊。

translations.literal: Later all commuted to paying labor wages; only going to the bridge remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later nearly all sentences were commuted to cash payments, though the bridge ceremony endured.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，御史鄭道寧言：「納米贖罪，朝廷寬典，乃軍儲倉拘繫罪囚，無米輸納，自去年二月至今，死者九十六人。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, Censor Zheng Daoning said: "Rice-payment commutation of crime is a court lenient measure—yet the Military Grain Storehouse detains criminal prisoners; with no rice to pay in, from last year's second month until now, ninety-six have died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2, Censor Zheng Daoning said: "Paying rice to commute one's sentence is a lenient policy—yet the military grain depots hold prisoners who cannot pay, and ninety-six have died since the second month of last year alone.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎俞士吉嘗奏：「囚無米者，請追納於原籍，匠仍輸作，軍仍備操，若非軍匠，則遣還所隸州縣追之。」

translations.literal: Criminal Affairs Section official Yu Shiji once memorialized: "For prisoners without rice, please pursue payment in their native place; artisans still deliver labor, soldiers still maintain drills—if neither soldier nor artisan, send back to their subordinate prefecture and county to pursue it."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji of the Ministry of Punishments memorialized: "Let those without rice pay at home—artisans should keep working, soldiers keep drilling; others should be returned to their home counties for collection."

sentences.zh: 詔從其奏。

translations.literal: An edict followed his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 初制流罪三等，視地遠近，邊衛充軍有定所。

translations.literal: The initial system had three grades of exile, depending on distance of place; border-garrison military exile had fixed destinations.
translations.idiomatic: The original code distinguished three grades of exile by distance; military exile to border garrisons had fixed destinations.

sentences.zh: 蓋降死一等，唯流與充軍為重。

translations.literal: For reducing death one grade, only exile and military exile were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Among penalties one step below death, only exile and military exile counted as severe.

sentences.zh: 然《名例律》稱二死三流各同為一減。

translations.literal: Yet the General Principles statute says the two deaths and three exiles each alike count as one reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the General Principles statute treats the two capital penalties and three exile grades alike as a single commutation.

sentences.zh: 如二死遇恩赦減一等，即流三千里，流三等以《大誥》減一等，皆徒五年。

translations.literal: For example, the two deaths encountering grace amnesty reduced one grade becomes exile three thousand li; the exile's three grades under the Grand Pronouncements reduced one grade—all penal servitude five years.
translations.idiomatic: When a capital sentence was commuted by amnesty it became three-thousand-li exile; under the Grand Pronouncements each exile grade was further reduced to five years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 犯流罪者，無不減至徒罪矣。

translations.literal: Those committing exile crimes—none failed to be reduced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: In practice every exile sentence was further reduced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 故三流常設而不用。

translations.literal: Thus the three exiles were constantly set forth yet not used.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the three exile grades existed in law but went unused.

sentences.zh: 而充軍之例為獨重。

translations.literal: Yet the military-exile precedent alone was uniquely heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Only military exile remained uniquely harsh.

sentences.zh: 律充軍凡四十六條，《諸司職掌》內二十二條，則洪武間例，皆律所不載者。

translations.literal: Statutory military exile totaled forty-six articles; within the Duties of the Various Offices twenty-two articles—Hongwu-era precedents, all not recorded in the statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Code listed forty-six articles on military exile; the Duties of the Various Offices added twenty-two Hongwu precedents absent from the Code itself.

sentences.zh: 其嘉靖二十九年條例，充軍凡二百十三條，與萬曆十三年所定大略相同。

translations.literal: The Jiajing twenty-ninth-year regulations—military exile totaled two hundred thirteen articles, broadly the same as that fixed in Wanli thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing's twenty-ninth-year regulations listed 213 articles on military exile, nearly identical to Wanli 13.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年定，應充軍者，大理寺審訖，開付陝西司，本部置立文簿，注姓名、年籍、鄉貫，依南北籍編排甲為二冊，一進內府，一付該管百戶，領去充軍。

translations.literal: Fixed in Hongwu twenty-six: those due for military exile, after the Court of Judicial Review concluded, were issued to the Shaanxi Bureau; the ministry established ledgers noting name, age-register, and native place; arranged by north-south register into two volumes of roster A—one advanced to the inner palace, one given to the controlling company officer to take away for military exile.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26, after the Court of Judicial Review ruled, a man's dossier went to the Shaanxi Bureau. The ministry recorded name, age, and native place, rostered him north or south in duplicate—one copy to court, one to his company officer—and sent him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如浙江，河南，山東，陝西，山西，北平，福建，直隸應天、廬州、鳳陽、淮安、揚州、蘇州、松江、常州、和州、滁州、徐州人，發雲南、四川屬衛；

translations.literal: For example persons of Zhejiang, Henan, Shandong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Beiping, Fujian, direct-administered Yingtian, Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Hezhou, Chuzhou, Xuzhou—dispatched to garrisons subordinate to Yunnan and Sichuan;
translations.idiomatic: Men from Zhejiang, Henan, Shandong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Beiping, Fujian, and the prefectures of Yingtian, Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Hezhou, Chuzhou, and Xuzhou were sent to garrisons in Yunnan and Sichuan;

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣，四川，廣東，廣西，直隸太平、甯國、池州、徽州、廣德、安慶人，發北平、大寧、遼東屬衛。

translations.literal: Jiangxi, Huguang, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, direct-administered Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Huizhou, Guangde, Anqing persons—dispatched to garrisons subordinate to Beiping, Daning, and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Men from Jiangxi, Huguang, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, and the prefectures of Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Huizhou, Guangde, and Anqing were posted to garrisons in Beiping, Daning, and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 有逃故，按籍勾補。

translations.literal: If there were flight or death, according to registers they were traced and replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Deserters and the dead were traced through the registers and replaced.

sentences.zh: 其後條例有發煙瘴地面、極邊沿海諸處者，例各不同。

translations.literal: Later regulations had dispatch to miasma ground, utmost border, and coastal places—each precedent differed.
translations.idiomatic: Later regulations dispatched men to miasma zones, extreme frontiers, and coasts—each with its own rules.

sentences.zh: 而軍有終身，有永遠。

translations.literal: And military service had lifelong and perpetual.
translations.idiomatic: Service might last for life or in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 永遠者，罰及子孫，皆以實犯死罪減等者充之。

translations.literal: Perpetual ones—punishment reached descendants; all were filled by those who actually committed capital crimes with reduced grades.
translations.idiomatic: Perpetual exile punished descendants too, applying to those whose capital sentences had been commuted.

sentences.zh: 明初法嚴，縣以千數，數傳之後，以萬計矣。

translations.literal: Early Ming law was strict; counties counted by thousands; after several transmissions, by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming enforcement was savage—thousands per county, tens of thousands within a few generations.

sentences.zh: 有丁盡戶絕，止存軍產者，或並無軍產，戶名未除者，朝廷歲遣御史清軍，有缺必補。

translations.literal: Where male heirs were exhausted and the household extinct, only military property remained—or even no military property yet the household name was not removed—the court annually sent censors to purify armies; any vacancy must be filled.
translations.idiomatic: When a line died out leaving only military property—or none, though the name lingered—the court sent annual commissioners to fill every gap.

sentences.zh: 每當勾丁，逮捕族屬、裏長，延及他甲，雞犬為之不寧。

translations.literal: Whenever conscripts were traced, kin and hamlet heads were arrested, extending to other tithing groups; even chickens and dogs for it knew no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Each muster seized kin and hamlet heads, spreading to neighboring wards until no household rested easy.

sentences.zh: 論者謂既減死罪一等，而法反加於刀鋸之上，如革除所遣謫，至國亡，戍籍猶有存者，刑莫慘於此矣。

translations.literal: Critics said that having already reduced capital crime one grade, the law instead was imposed above blades and saws—like those exiled in the purge reforms; until the state's fall, military registers still survived—no punishment more wretched than this.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that a sentence allegedly one step below death was worse than execution itself—Yongle's purge exiles still appeared on frontier rolls at the dynasty's fall. No penalty, they said, was crueler.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，有請開贖軍例者。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, some petitioned to open a military-exile ransom precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing's reign some proposed allowing military exiles to buy their way out.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「律聽贖者，徒杖以下小罪耳。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor said: "What the statute permits ransom for is only minor crimes of penal servitude and rods and canes.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor said: "Statutory commutation covers only penal servitude and beating.

sentences.zh: 死罪矜疑，乃減從謫發，不可贖。」

translations.literal: Capital crime treated with compassionate doubt is then reduced and banished accordingly—cannot be ransomed.
translations.idiomatic: Those spared death are exiled instead—they cannot buy their freedom.

sentences.zh: 御史周時亮復請廣贖例。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Shiliang again asked to broaden the ransom precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Shiliang petitioned again to broaden commutation.

sentences.zh: 部議審有力者銀十兩，得贖三年以上徒一年，稍有力者半之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: adjudged you li ten taels of silver could ransom one year from three years or more penal servitude; shao you li half that.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed ten taels for the prosperous to shave one year from a three-year sentence, and five for those of modest means.

sentences.zh: 而贖軍之議卒罷。

translations.literal: Yet the discussion of ransoming military exile in the end was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal to ransom military exile was dropped.

sentences.zh: 御史胡宗憲言：「南方之人不任兵革，其發充邊軍者，宜令納銀自贖。」

translations.literal: Censor Hu Zongxian said: "Southerners cannot bear weapons and armor; those dispatched as frontier soldiers should be ordered to pay silver to ransom themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Zongxian argued that southerners were ill suited to soldiering and that border exiles should be allowed to pay silver for release.

sentences.zh: 部議以為然，因擬納例以上。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that it was so, and accordingly drafted payment precedents for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry agreed and drafted rates accordingly.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈可設此例以待犯罪之人？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could one set this precedent awaiting those who commit crimes?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Are we to establish a tariff for future criminals?

sentences.zh: 復不允。

translations.literal: Again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again he refused.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，罷歲遣清軍御史，並於巡按，民獲稍安。

translations.literal: Wanli year two, the annually dispatched army-purifying censors were abolished and merged into touring inspectors; the people gained slight peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2 the yearly army-purging censors were abolished and their duties folded into the touring inspectors' brief, and the populace found modest relief.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐桓言：「死罪雜犯準徒充軍者，當如其例。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Huan said: "Those with capital crimes for miscellaneous offenses commuted to penal servitude then military exile should follow that precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Huan said that those whose capital offenses for mixed crimes were commuted to military exile should be treated accordingly.

sentences.zh: 給事中嚴用和請以大審可矜人犯，免其永戍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yan Yonghe asked that through the great review, offenders deserving pity be exempted from perpetual frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yonghe asked that prisoners found deserving pity in the great judicial review be spared perpetual frontier service.

sentences.zh: 皆不許。

translations.literal: All were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: All were denied.

sentences.zh: 而命法司定例：「奉特旨處發叛逆家屬子孫，止於本犯親枝內勾補，盡絕即與開豁。

translations.literal: Yet the throne ordered the judiciary to fix precedent: "Those rebel kin descendants dispatched by special edict—tracing and filling only within the offender's collateral branches; when utterly extinct then grant exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne ordered new rules: descendants of rebels banished by special edict would be traced only within the offender's collateral line and freed when the line died out.

sentences.zh: 若未經發遣而病故，免其勾補。

translations.literal: If not yet dispatched and died of illness, exempt their tracing and filling.
translations.idiomatic: If they died before dispatch, no successor would be seized.

sentences.zh: 其實犯死罪免死充軍者，以著伍後所生子孫替役，不許勾原籍子孫。

translations.literal: Those who actually committed capital crimes but were spared death for military exile—after enrollment in roster, descendants born afterward replace service; not permitted to trace descendants in the native register.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose capital sentences were commuted to military exile would be replaced by sons born after enrollment, not by relatives left at home.

sentences.zh: 其他充軍及發口外者，俱止終身。」

translations.literal: Other military exile and dispatch beyond the passes—all only for life.
translations.idiomatic: All other military exiles and banishments beyond the passes lasted only one lifetime.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，諭兵部：「編遣事宜，以千里為附近，二千五百里為邊衛，三千里外為邊遠，其極邊煙瘴以四千里外為率。

translations.literal: Chongzhen eleven, instructed the Ministry of War: "Matters of rostering and dispatch—take one thousand li as near, two thousand five hundred li as border garrison, beyond three thousand li as far border; the utmost border miasma at beyond four thousand li as standard.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 11 the throne told the Ministry of War: nearby exile meant within 1,000 li, border garrison 2,500 li, distant border beyond 3,000 li, and miasma-ridden extremes beyond 4,000 li.

sentences.zh: 止拘本妻，無妻則已，不許擅勾親鄰。

translations.literal: Only detain the proper wife; if no wife then stop; not permitted to arbitrarily trace kin and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Only the offender's own wife could be seized; if he had none, none could be taken—and neighbors and kin could not be dragged in.

sentences.zh: 如衰痼老疾，準發口外為民。」

translations.literal: If feeble with chronic illness and old age, approve dispatch beyond the passes as civilians."
translations.idiomatic: The aged and infirm could be banished beyond the passes as commoners.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又諭：「欲令引例充軍者，準其贖罪。」

translations.literal: Year fifteen, again instructed: "Those wishing to have military exile by precedent citation should be approved ransom of crime."
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 15 the throne said that those sent to the frontier under precedents should be allowed to commute their sentences.

sentences.zh: 時天下已亂，議卒不行。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven was already in disorder; the discussion in the end did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm was already in chaos, and the plan never took effect.

sentences.zh: 明制充軍之律最嚴，犯者亦最苦。

translations.literal: Ming system's military-exile law was strictest; offenders also suffered most bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Ming military exile was the harshest law in the code and the bitterest fate for those who suffered it.

sentences.zh: 親族有科斂軍裝之費，裏遞有長途押解之擾。

translations.literal: Kin had levies for military outfit expenses; the li relay had long-distance escort and delivery troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Kin paid levies for kit and transport; village relay officers endured the long march of escort duty.

sentences.zh: 至所充之衛，衛官必索常例。

translations.literal: Arriving at the garrison where they were conscripted, garrison officers must demand standing fees.
translations.idiomatic: At the receiving garrison, officers demanded their customary bribes.

sentences.zh: 然利其逃走，可幹沒口糧，每私縱之。

translations.literal: Yet profiting from their flight, one could embezzle ration grain; each time privately let them go.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officers profited from absconders—they could embezzle rations—and often looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 其後律漸弛，發解者不能十一。

translations.literal: Later the law gradually relaxed; those actually dispatched and delivered could not reach one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Enforcement slackened until fewer than one in ten exiles actually reached the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其發極邊者，長解輒賄兵部，持勘合至衛，虛出收管，而軍犯顧在家偃息云。

translations.literal: As for those dispatched to the utmost border, the chief escort bribed the Ministry of War, held the verification tally to the garrison, falsely issued receipt for custody—while the military offender rested at home in ease, they say.
translations.idiomatic: For the farthest postings, chief escorts bribed the Ministry of War, presented verification tallies to the garrison, recorded sham enlistments, and left the exile at home in comfort—or so it was said.
